spots.desc: A small club for about 50 people — positive atmosphere with Techno and Psy music or the accidental Old School Electro. Also, one of the less expensive venues with an according more alternative crowd.

spots.name: Deaf Shop
spots.desc: A small vinyl listening bar with a cozy atmosphere that seems to serve as a shop during the day. At night a curated selection of LPs and hosts events with guest DJs makes it a unique spot for music lovers in the city. It fits only a tiny crowd of about 30–50 people, so don't come too late! After midnight they will close the front gate to continue raving — don't worry, this is not a scheme to…

spots.name: Liquid Room
spots.desc: A full blown EDM club (House, Techno, and Trance) with regular international DJs. It features a lively bar experience with eclectic drinks for those guests willing to spend. Probably the largest of the clubs in Chiang Mai.

spots.name: Noise
spots.desc: A prominent and cozy Chinese Underground Techno Club, if that doesn't sound too racist. A dark venue with likewise darker kind of electronic music for a crowd that enjoys deep and experimental tunes.

spots.name: Red CNX
spots.desc: A western orientated club known for its energetic atmosphere with famous host DJs from time to time and electronic music genres like House and Techno. Young and hip. Due to its size (more than 150 people), it will need a decent crowd to be fun. Don't pay entrance if you are not 100% sure that there is a crowd inside, ready to let loose.

spots.name: Doi Chaang Coffee
spots.desc: Great coffee grown and roasted in the mountains. It is organic and the farmers own 50 percent of the company. They also make the Wild Thai Civet Coffee. Next to the coffee company there is a cafe where you can order a cup of coffee and also buy a bag of coffee beans. Also try their honey.

spots.name: Doi Nang Non
spots.desc: The silhouette of the mountain range takes the shape of a reclining woman with long hair when seen from certain angles. There is a viewpoint at Mae Chan from where the "sleeping lady" can be observed best in good weather. There are a number of caves and water courses in these karstic hills. Tum Luang and Khun Naam Nang Non, have been developed as tourist attractions.

spots.name: Doi Wawi
spots.desc: Chinese community in the northern part of Thailand. Wawi is one of the biggest tea-producing areas in Thailand. You can visit the village, taste the tea and buy some tea. It is also possible to visit the tea plantation.

spots.name: Golden Triangle
spots.local: Samliam Thongkum or สามเหลี่ยมทองคำ
spots.desc: The point where Thailand, Myanmar, and Laos meet. It used to be notorious for its drug trafficking until the Royal Thai government cleaned up the area and turned into a tourist destination.

spots.name: World's Tallest Flagpole
spots.desc: The Chiang Saen District is to have the world's tallest flagpole sometime in 2017. The pole will be 189 m tall, the equivalent of a 63-storey building. Its purpose is to promote Thainess and Thai identity. The flagpole will be in a park complete with a museum and a learning centre.

spots.name: Hall of Opium, Golden Triangle Park
spots.local: หอฝิ่นอุทยานสามเหลี่ยมทองคำ
spots.desc: One of the best museums in all Thailand and almost certainly the most interesting place to visit in the Golden Triangle, the Hall of Opium exhibits the history of opium around the world and in the area, the process of production, the effects of opium smoking and campaigns to eradicate and substitute the crop. There's even a tiny opium plantation inside! The hall describes itself as "edutainment"…

spots.name: House of Opium
spots.desc: A privately-run museum, associated with a souvenir shop, it is unrelated to and much smaller than the hall and lacks their sophisticated presentation. Lots of opium paraphernalia and information on the production process from beginning to end.

spots.name: Phra That Doi Pu Khao
spots.local: พระธาตุดอยปูเข้า
spots.desc: Believed to have been built by a king of Wiang Hirannakhon Ngoen Yang in mid-8th century. Remains of antiquities are in the Viharn with crumbled chedis.

spots.name: Sriwan
spots.desc: Clean, friendly and tasty restaurant on the riverbank, offering a wide menu of all the usual Thai and Western dishes. Noodle and rice dishes start from 40 baht.

spots.name: Aviary
spots.desc: With around 100 local species such as parrots (English is spoken!) and hornbills.

spots.name: City Pillar Shrine/Lak Mueang (Thai)
spots.desc: The spiritual centre of the city and province. A Lak Mueang (Thai) or 'City Pillar Shrine' is a golden pillar, which represents the tutelary deity of each province of Thailand, housed inside an impressively designed structure. This shrine was designed by the Thai Fine Arts Department, in a Khymer-style.

spots.name: Houseboats
spots.desc: Once a symbol of Phitsanulok, only a few of these are left on the river and some now function as restaurants and cafes.

spots.name: King Naresuan Shrine and Wang Chan Palace Ruin
spots.desc: King Naresuan was one of the great Thai kings who liberated Ayutthaya Kingdom from the Burmese in the 16th century. This shrine commemorates his life. A small white building contains the statue of the King. Surrounding the shrine are the ruins of the king's palace birthplace.

spots.name: Wat Phra Sri Rattana Mahathat
spots.desc: This is the most important temple in Phitsanulok and is the home of the famous Phra Buddha Chinnarat, one of the most revered Buddha figures in Thailand. The temple is host to a large fair every January. There is also a small market on the ground, where people offer souvenirs and local food. Connected to the temple ground of Wat Yai is the Nang Phaya Temple. There you can get a traditional Thai…

spots.name: Wat Ratburana
spots.desc: This wat is best known for its very old and tall chedi. According to legend this was constructed in the 15th century to house the ashes of the King of Sukhothai's two brothers. There is also the usual Thai temple buildings, plus, a small museum, and a boat used by King Chulalongkorn.

spots.name: Night Bazaar
spots.desc: Offers lots of tourist type food options plus after dinner shopping with the usual night market items.

spots.name: Topland Mall
spots.desc: Shopping mall with standard chain restaurant fare. There is a Tesco-Lotus downstairs for self catering and other essentials.

spots.name: Kuai Tiao Hoi Kha
spots.local: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวห้อยขา
spots.desc: Very popular noodle restaurant by the riverside. "Kuai Tiao" means noodle and "Hoi Kha" to dangle one's legs, referring to the fact that you can dangle your legs in the air while sitting there. May be difficult to find a seat during lunchtime.

spots.name: Bubbletea Kiosk
spots.desc: A small bubble tea stall / kiosk offering really cheap, but tasty bubble tea. Open throughout the day.

spots.name: It's a Cake
spots.desc: Great cakes and good sandwiches, pasta, and Thai dishes. Internet access.

spots.name: The Pista
spots.desc: Great little coffee shop mainly visited by young local students, with surprisingly good coffee and a quiet environment, good seating, and aircon. Free Wifi.

spots.name: Ban Lipa Yai
spots.desc: This village grows high quality fruits, including rambutan, durian, mangosteen and the famed langsat.

spots.name: Bang Rak Beach
spots.desc: Also known as “Big Buddha Beach”, in northeast Samui, Big Buddha offers visitors good swimming and lovely views. The area has developed a lot and there are now plenty of restaurants, shops, and bars.

spots.name: Bophut Beach
spots.desc: In the north of the island, is a popular starting point for diving tours. The place isn't in any way as developed as Chaweng but there are still plenty of restaurants, shops, and bars.

spots.name: Chaweng Beach
spots.desc: The major beach on Ko Samui and one that has developed tremendously since the early 1990s. The beach used to be home to just a sprinkle of wooden bungalows but now the place is swamped with hotels, pizza joints, pubs, and go-go bars. Samui’s nightlife is becoming legendary but unfortunately does not always attract the highest standard of tourist. Chaweng’s once hippie-only backpackers have given…

spots.name: Choeng Mon Beach
spots.desc: In the northeast corner of Samui just 10 minutes from Chaweng. Unlike the latter, it is a perfect place for relaxing.

spots.name: Grandmother and Grandfather Rocks
spots.desc: These odd-looking rocks at the south end of Lamai Beach bear a striking resemblance to male and female genitalia and they have turned into one of the island’s biggest attractions. For those who would like to hear a legend or two surrounding the rocks, they need only ask a local.

spots.name: Hin Lat Waterfall
spots.desc: Easily accessible by car. Some of the numerous tiny levels have a large basin for swimmers.

spots.name: Lamai Beach
spots.desc: Like Chaweng, Lamai has been transformed from a hippie hangout into a fun, party place packed out with bars and exciting nightlife. The beach though, is still in better condition than Chaweng and the place doesn’t get quite so crowded. But if it’s a quiet relaxing location you are after, then the tourist downtown, known as Lamai Beach, won’t be the ideal place for you. The quieter northeast end…

spots.name: Mae Nam Beach
spots.desc: This quiet beach, in the north of the island, is decent enough for swimming and sunbathing especially for families with children due to the shallow water.

spots.name: Na Mueang Waterfall
spots.desc: A local road leads to the Na Mueang 1 Waterfall just off Rte 4169. A walk of about 30 minutes ends up at the more scenic Na Mueang 2 Waterfall. Purple rocks surround the stream of water, which gushes in from an impressive height of around 79 m.

spots.name: Old House
spots.desc: This Chinese-style house, almost 200 years old, hints at Samui's distant cultural past. Grandpa Si and Grandma Maen Hancharoen, the present owners, open the house to visitors.

spots.name: Monkey Shows
spots.desc: These shows can be observed at the open-air theatre on the main road behind Bophut beach. The entertainment also includes performing elephants. However, the capturing and training of otherwise wild animals is at best ethically questionable.

spots.name: Samui Aquarium and Tiger Zoo
spots.desc: The undersea world of the aquarium has an amazing collection of tropical fish and other vibrant aquatic animals such as turtles and colourful coral. The tiger zoo is home to Bengal tigers and leopards. For those who are daring enough, they can have their photograph taken with the animals.

spots.name: Samui Butterfly Garden / Insect Museum
spots.desc: There is a huge collection of butterflies, some a quarter of a metre wide. In the nearby Insect Museum, you can see a variety of rare bugs and a bee house.

spots.name: Laem Sor Pagoda Ko Samui
spots.desc: This chedi (pagoda) at Laem Sor temple is one of the most important shrines on Ko Samui. The structure with its yellow tiles which gives off a golden aura is quite impressive.

spots.name: Wat Khunaram Ko Samui
spots.desc: This temple is the island’s most famous temple for its mummified monk on display. The mummy sits upright in a glass casket and devotees offer it flowers and incense. The mummy is in fact the body of a very revered former abbot of the temple who was also a meditation master who was able to predict his own death.

spots.name: Ten Stars Samui Art Party
spots.desc: A recurring cultural event bringing together art lovers, local Thai and international artists, and their artwork. The annual event, hosted at various resorts and other venues, focus on building the art community on Ko Samui, with presentations by featured artists.

spots.name: Koh Samui THA Midnight Run
spots.desc: The Ko Samui Midnight Run is a charity run organized by the Thai Hotel Association (THA) and the Thai Association of Ko Samui (TAKS). It is a yearly event usually held in March. With up to 2000 participants, the run is one of the biggest on Samui and in Thailand. Participants will run 5 or 10 km around the buzzy and lively streets of Chaweng Beach. The first run was held in 2013.

spots.name: Samui Regatta
spots.desc: A sailing race held every year. The tournament is internationally known and competitors come from as far away as Australia, Singapore, Japan and China. The event began in 2002.
spots.price: Entry fee, 22,500 baht; each crew member, 5,500 baht

spots.name: Samui Triathlon
spots.desc: The International Triathlon Union organizes this event every year. This event draws more than five hundred participants from around the world.

spots.name: Hat Noppharat Thara - Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติหาดนพรัตน์ธารา – หมู่เกาะพีพี
spots.desc: Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park has an area of 242,437 rai (38,790 ha) of which 200,849 rai (32,136 ha) is sea. There are three distinctive kinds of forest here: moist evergreen forests, mangrove forests, and peat swamp forests.

spots.name: Su-san Hoi (Shell Cemetery)
spots.local: สุสานหอย
spots.desc: Once a large freshwater swamp, the habitat of diverse mollusks of about 2 cm in size, Su-san Hoi features a slab formed from a huge number of embedded mollusks which can be dated to approximately 40 million years ago. With changes on the surface of the earth, seawater flooded the freshwater swamp and the limestone elements in the seawater enveloped the submerged mollusks resulting in a…

spots.name: Than Bok Khorani National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติธารโบกขรณี
spots.desc: The park covers an area of 121 km2. The landscape is dominated by a series of limestone mountains, evergreen forests, mangrove forests, and numerous islands. The main flora is evergreen forest, peat swamp forest, strand forest, and mangrove forest, as well as various types of marine flora. Other attractions include: Than Bokkhorani (ธารโบกขรณี) which is home to various flowing streams and…

spots.name: Namtok Ron Khlong Thom
spots.local: น้ำตกร้อนคลองท่อม
spots.desc: An area of hot springs in a shady forest. The temperature is at 40-50 degrees Celsius. The hot springs and cool streams converge on a slope to form cascades of warm water.

spots.name: Mu Ko Lanta National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติหมู่เกาะลันตา
spots.desc: Covering a total area of 152 km2, Mu Ko Lanta National Park is in Amphoe Ko Lanta and consists of many islands. Some major islands are Ko Lanta Yai, Ko Lanta Noi, Ko Taleng Beng, as well as, other surrounding islands like Mu Ko Ha, Mu Ko Rok, and Ko Ngai.

spots.name: Jui Tui and Put Jaw Temples
spots.desc: Put Jaw is the oldest Chinese Taoist temple in Phuket, built over 200 years ago and dedicated to the Goddess of Mercy (Kwun Im), while the adjacent and connected Jui Tui is its larger, more modern annex. If you have a question that is puzzling you, ask it and throw the two red mango-shaped pieces in front of the altar in the air: if they land same side up, the answer is "no". If they land…

spots.name: Khao Rang
spots.local: เขารัง
spots.desc: A great view of Phuket Town, the southern part of the island, and some of the offshore islands, can be obtained by going to the top of Khao Rang Hill, on the town's northwest border. There are also several restaurants featuring spectacular views of the city, a health park for exercise enthusiasts, and a comfortable, expanse of grass at the top with a bronze statue of Phraya Ratsada Nupradit, the…

spots.name: Old Phuket
spots.local: ย่านเมืองเก่าภูเก็ต
spots.desc: The beginning of the tin boom in the 19th century led to construction of many fine mansions and shops that are still well-preserved. The architectural style, typical of the region, is described as Sino-Portuguese and has a strong Mediterranean character. Shops present a very narrow face to the street, but stretch back a long way. Many, especially on Dibuk Rd, have old wooden doors with Chinese…
spots.addr: Dibuk Rd, Phang Nga Rd, Yaowarat Rd, Thalang Rd, Krabi Rd

spots.name: Phuket Cultural Center
spots.local: ศูนย์ศิลปวัฒนธรรมจังหวัดภูเก็ต
spots.desc: History as well as the arts and culture of Phuket, such as houses, ways of life, and utensils of the city of Thalang in ancient times. The library collects books on Phuket's history and culture. For a group of visitors who need a guided tour, address a letter of request to the Phuket Cultural Center.

spots.name: Phuket Culture Museum
spots.desc: It's very informative. Phuket's history is told in pictures.

spots.name: Phuket Zoo
spots.local: สวนสัตว์ภูเก็ต
spots.desc: The zoo contains a collection of Asian and African mammals and birds. Elephant and crocodile shows every day. Caution, Phuket Zoo may be closed permanently.

spots.name: Saphan Hin
spots.local: สะพานหิน
spots.desc: A land reclamation project provided abundant new land now used for parks and public facilities at Saphan Hin, located where Phuket Rd meets the sea in Phuket Town. In the circle is the Tin Mining Monument, shaped like a large drill bit, dedicated to the memory of Captain Edward Thomas Miles, the Australian who brought the first tin dredge to Phuket in 1909. The monument was built in 1969 on the…

spots.name: Thai Village and Orchid Farm
spots.local: หมู่บ้านไทยและสวนกล้วยไม้ภูเก็ต
spots.desc: Serves daily a typical southern Thai lunch followed by a spectacular cultural show including Thai dances, Thai boxing, southern customs and elephants. Handicrafts are also on display. The complex also houses a dining hall decorated with over 20,000 varieties of orchids and tropical trees. Digestion is aided by the lilting sounds of Thai classical and folk music played on traditional instruments.…

spots.name: Thaihua Museum
spots.desc: In an old Chinese language school, this museum tells the history of Chinese immigrants on Phuket.

spots.name: Wat Mongkol Nimit
spots.desc: A classical Thai-style temple with a soaring roof and lots of colourful glass tiling.

spots.name: Chamber of Secrets @ BaanTeelanka
spots.desc: An exciting room escape game at Baan Teelanka, the Upside Down House and the garden maze.

spots.name: Raintree Spa Phuket
spots.desc: Has a variety of spa treatments that include traditional Thai massage, body treatments, facials, and spa packages.

spots.name: Weekend Market
spots.desc: Endless stalls with the cheapest of Thai souvenirs and counterfeit goods. Food court is large and is alone worth a visit.

spots.name: Central Festival
spots.desc: Phuket's branch of the Thai department store chain, also selling anything and everything, but now in air-con comfort and a zero added to the price tag. It's still probably cheaper than the street markets at the beaches. The food section offers a large variety of Western products and the fresh products seem to be of better quality than Big C or Tesco Lotus. Prices are much higher though.

spots.name: Ocean and Robinsons
spots.desc: Robinsons is a big department store, and there is a Tops Supermarket, as well as McDonald's, KFC, and other regrettable Western imports.

spots.name: Naka Weekend Market
spots.desc: Numerous stalls sell a variety of meats, vegetables, noodles, fruits, and sweets that can fill a stomach for a handful of baht.

spots.name: China Inn Cafe & Restaurant
spots.desc: Dinner in beautiful historic Sino-Portuguese building in Phuket old town with romantic atmosphere. Thai and European food. Open: M-W, 11:00-18:00; Th-Sa, 11:00-23:00. Closed Su.

spots.name: Ruamjai Vegan Restaurant
spots.desc: A locally-run restaurant with friendly staff serving delicious all-vegetarian food. The prices are very reasonable. A plate of white/brown rice with two or more dishes from the buffet of about 15 different courses is around 25-35 baht. Try also locally-made fresh juices, 10 baht each. Popular among locals; it can be crowded around mealtimes. One of 3 vegetarian restaurants in close to the local…

spots.name: Siam Bakery
spots.desc: French-run bakery offering pastries and drinks (~50 baht) in pleasant air-con surroundings.

spots.name: Kota Khao Mun Kai
spots.desc: Very nice clean local place to get a specialty of the region, Khao Mun Kai - chicken with rice. The owners are very friendly to foreigners and will help show you how to eat it.
spots.price: 60 baht for food, 10 for a drink (Nov 2017)

spots.name: Phuketiquette
spots.desc: Home of arguably the best coffee in Phuket, and probably the best value for money in Phuket Town. Great mix of Thai and international food, and a very friendly, young owner who will offer you great advice on what to see and do while in Phuket. Free Wi-Fi, DVD club.

spots.name: Kra Jok See
spots.desc: Serving Thai cuisine tailored to Western palates, the restaurant sheds its inhibitions at 22:00 when the tables are pushed back and hostesses pull guests onto the floor for dancing, which is heaps of fun.

spots.name: Raya
spots.desc: Thai cuisine, southern style. Popular dishes such as crab meat curry served with white noodles. Shrimp with tamarind sauce. Pork with garlic and black pepper. Fish with tamarind sauce. Salty pork. Fish with yellow curry and vegetables.

spots.name: China House
spots.desc: Chinese tea and other drinks in an impeccably restored shop house that doubles as an art gallery. On the expensive side though, with drinks 50-100 baht.

spots.name: Coffee Max
spots.desc: Small, friendly coffee shop offering hot and cold coffee and tea drinks and a selection of pastries and cakes. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Michael's Bar
spots.desc: Owned by a British expat, a friendly, low-key place to grab a few drinks at a reasonable price. Has Wi-Fi and a PC for customer use, free for the first 20 minutes. Good happy hour prices.

spots.name: O'Malley's Pub
spots.desc: Phuket Town's oldest pub. Good selection of beers, wines, and spirits at reasonable prices. Free pool, darts and Wi-Fi. All sport shown on two large flat screen TVs. Good selection of food and bar snacks. Recently opened hostel above the bar with dorm beds starting at 190 baht per night, the cheapest in Phuket Town. Currently closed.

spots.name: Smile Cafe
spots.desc: Run by a friendly young Thai couple who make a great ice-blended coffee or green tea.

spots.name: Hat Yai Park
spots.local: สวนสาธารณะเทศบาลเมืองหาดใหญ่
spots.desc: The city's municipal park is 6 km from the city centre. It is a major recreational centre for the people of Hat Yai and surrounding areas. The park is full of beautiful flowering plants, with a pavilion in the middle of the pond, aviarium, and food stalls. At the foot of the hill near the aviarium stands the statue of King Rama V. There is a Brahman shrine at the hilltop. And at the southern…

spots.name: Hat Yai Cable Car
spots.desc: There are two stations: one at Phra Buddha Mongkol Maharaj (พระพุทธมงคลมหาราช) and the other at Thao Maha Phrom (ท้าวมหาพรหม). The second phase will add two more stations at the playground and Guanyin statue, connecting four stations altogether. There is also a tram service running between the cable car station and the Hat Yai Ice Dome during 10:00-17:00 for 50 baht. A one-way cable car ride…
spots.price: Round trip 200 baht, 100 baht for Thais

spots.name: Khlong Hae Floating Market
spots.local: ตลาดน้ำคลองแห
spots.desc: The first floating market in south Thailand. Sells mainly local foods.

spots.name: Sino-Portuguese Townhouses
spots.desc: These old Peranakan-inspired houses have been re-painted in vivid colours.

spots.name: Songkhla Central Mosque
spots.local: มัสยิดกลางประจำจังหวัดสงขลา
spots.desc: This beautiful grand mosque is 400 m off the road from Hat Yai to Songkhla.
spots.addr: 352 Lopburi Ramesuan Rd, Moo 10, Khlong Hae

spots.name: Stainless Steel Pagoda
spots.local: พระมหาธาตุเจดีย์ไตรภพไตรมงคล Phra Maha Chedi Traipob Traimongkhon
spots.desc: This unique pagoda was made of stainless steel to celebrate King Bhumibol Adulyadej's 60th year on the throne.
spots.addr: Moo 8 Ban Nai Rai, Poonnakan Rd

spots.name: Wat Hat Yai Nai
spots.local: วัดหาดใหญ่ใน
spots.desc: The temple is the site of a large reclining Buddha measuring 35m long, 15m tall, and 10m wide, named Phra Phuttha Hattha Mongkhon, believed to be the third-largest reclining Buddha in the world, and revered by both Thai and foreign tourists.

spots.name: Khao Nam Khang Historic Tunnel
spots.local: อุโมงค์ประวัติศาสตร์เขาน้ำค้าง
spots.desc: This large, long man-made tunnel was once inhabited by Communist insurgents. It is three levels deep and contains several rooms. Entry fee for foreigners is 150 baht.

spots.name: Khu Khut Waterfowl Park
spots.local: อุทยานนกน้ำคูขุด
spots.desc: You can hire a boat for birdwatching (200 baht/hr) and have a pleasant meal at the restaurants beside the serene lake. The best time to visit is during Dec-Mar.

spots.name: Thale Noi Waterfowl Reserve
spots.local: เขตห้ามล่าสัตว์ป่าทะเลน้อย
spots.desc: Home to staggering 287 bird species. The best time for bird watching and seeing a sea of blooming pink water lilies is during Jan-Apr. Go early in the morning to avoid strong sun. A boat ride costs 500 baht and takes about 1½ hr.

spots.name: Ton Nga Chang Waterfall
spots.local: น้ำตกโตนงาช้าง
spots.desc: The waterfall is in the Ton Nga Chang Wildlife Sanctuary. It is one of the beautiful waterfalls in the south, about 26 km from the city. This waterfall has seven levels. The third level is the most beautiful and is named after the waterfall. At the third level the stream separates into two, resembling an elephant's tusks. One can hire a tuk-tuk to the waterfall for two to three hours at 300-400…

spots.name: Chinese New Year
spots.local: เทศกาลตรุษจีน
spots.desc: Usually fall in Jan or Feb depending on the Chinese calendar. With a sizeable Thai-Chinese population, Chinese New Year is celebrated everywhere in Hat Yai especially in the city center. The Chinese New Year is on 5 Feb 2019.

spots.name: Hat Yai Midnight Songkran
spots.local: เทศกาลสงกรานต์หาดใหญ่
spots.desc: The festival marks Thai New Year, which is traditionally celebrated during 13-15 Apr. The most prominent part of the festival is blessing people with sprinkles of water. As you can guess, this devolves into massive water fights. The main activities are held near/around Odean Shopping Mall and Lee Garden Plaza, including foam party, free concert, and Songkran beauty contest.

spots.name: Hat Yai Vegetarian Festival
spots.local: เทศกาลกินเจหาดใหญ่; Nine Emperor Gods Festival
spots.desc: A yearly event held during the ninth month of the Chinese calendar (usually in October). Observed mostly by Chinese and, increasingly, some Thais.

spots.name: Loi Krathong
spots.local: วันลอยกระทง
spots.desc: Festival to pay respect to the river by floating beautifully decorated krathong (กระทง). It usually incorporates a Nang Noppamas (นางนพมาศ) beauty competition where contestants dress in Thai traditional costume. The festival is held on the full moon night of the twelfth lunar month.

spots.name: Tham Bun Duean Sip
spots.local: เทศกาลทำบุญเดือนสิบ
spots.desc: A Southern Thai tradition held in/around October (the full-moon day of the tenth lunar month). The main purpose is to make merit for their ancestors. There are specific foods made for this. Business may close for the day.

spots.name: Cinema
spots.desc: Movie tickets in Thailand are more affordable than in Western countries. There are multiplexes and an IMAX theatre at Hatyai Cineplex on 5F of CentralFestival. The other venue is at Diana Cineplex on 5F of Diana.

spots.name: Thai Massage
spots.desc: No trip to Thailand would be complete without a Thai massage and Hat Yai is one of the best places to get one. Some of the many good places would be Garden Home Hotel or Hat Yai Central Hotel. The rooms are nicely decorated and provide a soothing environment to go with a good massage. Ask the doorman at any good hotel for a recommendation if you want to avoid the more dodgy places.

spots.name: ASEAN Trade Market
spots.local: ตลาดเปิดท้าย Talat Poet Tai
spots.desc: Wide market famous for second-hand designer clothing, bags, and shoes, but interesting locally-designed new clothes and some vintage decorative stuff can be found here as well. Lots of food stalls inside.

spots.name: Kim Yong Market
spots.local: ตลาดกิมหยง
spots.desc: This is the most attractive place for shopping. There are plenty of foods, home appliances, chocolates, cosmetics, watches, CD games.

spots.name: Suntisuk Market
spots.local: สันติสุข
spots.desc: The famous market sells electric appliances, gadgets, gaming consoles, IT devices and accessories, clothes, shoes, bags, cosmetics, imported food.

spots.name: Central Hatyai
spots.desc: It's one of the largest shopping complexes outside Bangkok. You can find fashion clothes, many restaurants and cafes (including After You Dessert Cafe), Hatyai Cineplex with 10 cinemas, bowling alley, karaoke, all major banks, Tops Market, IT and electronics, telco service centers, and more.

spots.name: Hatyai Village
spots.desc: Community mall. Petrol station, Starbucks, KFC, Burger King, Swensen's, food court, Uniqlo, Mr.DIY, Tops Supermarket, Lotus's Go Fresh, etc.

spots.name: Lee Gardens Plaza
spots.desc: The most popular mall for Thai teenagers. Restaurants include Sizzler, Swensen's, McDonald's, and Fuji among others. Shops inside sell books, clothes, mobile phones, and souvenirs. There is a multiplex cinema and a games complex which also includes karaoke booths.

spots.name: Siam Nakarin Complex
spots.desc: Office supplies, furniture, restaurants, food court, IT/mobile phones, and other small shops.

spots.name: Tesco Lotus Hat Yai 1
spots.desc: A large supermarket that sells food, clothes, household items. There are also restaurants and smaller shops just outside the main supermarket.

spots.name: Chok Dee Tae Tiam
spots.local: โชคดีแต่เตี้ยม
spots.desc: One of the most famous dim sum restaurants in Hat Yai. The restaurant fills up fast, so go early to ensure a table. If you order bak kut teh, you'll get refilled constantly.
spots.price: Dim sum: 16 baht/basket; Bak kut teh: 80/250 baht for small/large bowl

spots.name: Bang Farang Restaurant
spots.local: ร้านอาหารบังฝรั่ง
spots.desc: Nice small cosy restaurant at a walking distance from the bus station, ASEAN Market, or Green Way market. Halal, genuine Thai food (spicy, not sweet Malay cuisine). Excellent kaeng som. Serves fresh fruit juices and coffee. Free Wi-Fi for patrons. The cook/owner is married to a Muslim Frenchman. You can usually meet him on Saturdays.

spots.name: Decha Fried Chicken
spots.local: ไก่ทอดเดชา
spots.desc: Muslim fried chicken restaurant. Also serve seafood, Thai, Isaan food.

spots.name: Cha-Chak Forseen
spots.local: ชาชักฟอร์ซีน
spots.desc: Its extensive menu includes grilled chicken/salmon steak, beef skewers, murtabak, savory/sweet roti, teh tarik, shaved ice, etc.

spots.name: Hamid Restaurant
spots.desc: Nice, clean, and good halal food. There are a couple of other Muslim restaurants nearby.

spots.name: Namaste Hatyai
spots.desc: Indian-Thai restaurant. Chicken biryani/murtabak, roti/chapati, lassi, and more. (No pork or beef served.) Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Seoul Korean BBQ Restaurant
spots.desc: Korean barbecue all-you-can-eat buffet including drinks and ice-creams.

spots.name: 33 Buffet Restaurant
spots.desc: The hotel has a top floor restaurant with panoramic views of the city. It offers an excellent all-you-can-eat buffet at lunch and dinner.

spots.name: 192 Rat Na
spots.local: 192 ราดหน้า อาหารตามสั่ง
spots.desc: Good Chinese food served here and very busy but worth waiting for some good fried stuff. Fried rice a specialty.

spots.name: Daothiam
spots.local: ดาวเทียม
spots.desc: Friendly staff and tasty breakfasts, Thai, and vegetarian food. Grab a pad Thai and Chang beer among a collection of framed world currency.

spots.name: Nai Roo Restaurant
spots.local: ร้านอาหารในรู
spots.desc: This hidden gem of a small Thai-Chinese restaurant may fill up quickly during meal time. Try fried popiah, tom yam omelette, fish dishes.

spots.name: Nakorn Nai
spots.local: นครใน
spots.desc: A stylish restaurant with free Wi-Fi. They serve very tasty Western food such as pasta and pizza, Thai food, and Muslim food such as roti for reasonable prices.

spots.name: Ta-kun
spots.local: ร้านตา-ขุน
spots.desc: If you're looking for cheap and good local food, try this small and very friendly little spot.

spots.name: Gäp's Garten German Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves authentic German food and beer (Erdinger, Warsteiner, Weihenstephan, and Köstritzer) for reasonable prices. Best to book a table in advance as it is usually quite full.

spots.name: Co Art
spots.desc: A cafe-style place to hang-out in the evenings. There is a live band almost every day covering internationally-known songs.

spots.name: Living Room
spots.desc: At the site of the now-defunct Monkey Club. It's a nice place with fairly quiet atmosphere, and no longer a nightclub.

spots.name: Oceania
spots.desc: A beautiful open-air restaurant and bar set on 2 floors with a landscaped garden of waterfalls and palms, and soft lighting. The kitchen is open until well after 02:00, serving decent Thai food at around 100 baht a dish. A large Heineken is 90 baht, with draft available also. The theme is quiet and romantic, ideal after an hour or two in the disco nearby. Live acoustic music is inflicted on…
spots.hours: Closes when last customer leaves, about 04:00

spots.name: Post Laser Disc
spots.desc: Air-conditioned and pool. Best band in town playing from 21:00 onwards. Farang hangout.

spots.name: Sunrise Coffee
spots.local: หอมกลิ่นกาแฟ
spots.desc: A nice little coffee shop offering a variety of coffee blends and smoothies; very cosy atmosphere.

spots.name: The Swan
spots.desc: Nice atmosphere with books and 2 TVs with UBC cable. A slight British pub feel.

spots.name: The West Side Saloon
spots.desc: Can get crowded and very noisy. They have a good bar food menu. The only pub/bar in town that writes the prices on the menu excluding service charge and VAT. Can be a surprise when you get the bill.

spots.name: Wat Langka
spots.local: วัดลังกา

spots.name: Wat Yan Sen
spots.local: วัดญาณเสน

spots.name: Wat Kudi Dao
spots.local: วัดกุฎีดาว

spots.name: Wat Chakkrawat
spots.local: วัดจักรวรรดิ์

spots.name: Wat Bot Rat Decha
spots.local: วัดโบสถ์ราชเดชะ

spots.name: Wat Ayothaya
spots.local: วัดอโยธยา

spots.name: Wat Dusidaram
spots.local: วัดดุสิดาราม

spots.name: Wat Wihan Khao
spots.local: วัดวิหารขาว

spots.name: Real Divers Pattaya PADI 5 Star IDC Center
Pattaya Paintball and Airsoft Park
spots.desc: Decent field; helpful English speaking manager.

spots.name: Tesco Lotus Pattaya Nuea
spots.desc: sells most things you need.

spots.name: Made In Thailand Night Bazaar
spots.desc: Despite the name, it is also open in mornings.

spots.name: Food Court of the Central Festival shopping mall
spots.desc: There are low-priced restaurants.

spots.name: Tesco Lotus North Pattaya Food Court
spots.desc: A good low-price place to eat.

spots.name: Nachrichtentreff
spots.desc: Serves pretty good Austrian food.

spots.name: Slice Pizza
spots.desc: An American-style pizzeria.

spots.name: Benihana
spots.desc: Japanese steakhouse restaurant chain.

spots.name: Breezeo
spots.desc: The restaurant serves excellent seafood and Thai dishes.
spots.addr: Royal Cliff Beach Hotel & Royal Cliff Beach Terrace

spots.name: Govindam 100% Pure Vegetarian & Jain Food
spots.desc: Indian vegetarian restaurant.

spots.name: Casino Club
spots.desc: A beer bar.

spots.name: Club Insomnia
spots.desc: House music, cheap drinks, late license, European DJ's.

spots.name: Benjamit Coffee
spots.desc: Great own brewed coffee, popular with expats

spots.name: Bake n Brew
spots.desc: Good coffee, cakes and breads. Partially air-conditioned

spots.name: Big C
spots.desc: Two locations. Hypermart, groceries, housewares, clothing.

spots.name: Landmark Plaza / TukCom
spots.desc: Shopping complex with SFC Cinema.

spots.name: Makro
spots.desc: Cheap bulk purchases.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: Eat in and takeaway food.

spots.name: Tops market CentralPlaza
spots.desc: Western and Thai foodstuffs; salad bar; deli; bakery.

spots.name: Bongkotch Restaurant
spots.local: ร้านอาหารบงกช
spots.desc: Popular Thai restaurant with good food and low prices.

spots.name: Dan Kwian
spots.desc: Famous for its rough textures and rust-like pottery glazes.

spots.name: Prasat Hin Phanom Wan
spots.desc: Khmer stupa built of sandstone.

spots.name: Wat Sala Loi
spots.desc: Chapel shaped like a Chinese junk.

spots.name: Jogging
spots.desc: Landscaped jogging park near the military base.

spots.name: Permaculture Children's House
spots.desc: Educational center teaching to work with nature.

spots.name: Thai Massage School of Chiang Mai
spots.desc: A government-registered school of Thai massage.

spots.name: The Lost Book Shop
spots.desc: Large collection of used books. Fiction and non-fiction.

spots.name: On The Road Books
spots.desc: Small bookstore with a nice selection of used books.

spots.name: Sanpakhoi Market
spots.desc: Produces, meat, food stalls, and much more at local prices.

spots.name: Anchan Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Excellent vegetarian food.

spots.name: Vegan Society
spots.desc: Vegan restaurant as well as a homestay.

spots.name: Salsa Kitchen
spots.desc: Mexican restaurant.

spots.name: Akha Ama
spots.desc: Moved to this new location from the Santitham area.

spots.name: Akha Ama Phrasingh

spots.desc: Good Thai food and great view looking onto Hat Yai.
