spots.desc: The fair takes place annually from the 12th day of the waxing moon to the 4th day of the waning moon in the 12th month of the lunar calendar. It is held on the grounds of Phra Pathom Chedi. At night, various entertainments are provided.

spots.name: Loy Krathong Festival
spots.local: งานประเพณีลอยกระทง
spots.desc: It is held annually on the 15th day of the waxing moon in the 12th month of the lunar calendar (November). The festival is held at Sanam Chan Palace, and features beauty pageants, Krathong contests, hanging lantern contests, and local entertainment, among others.

spots.name: Flying Ice Cream
spots.desc: Ice cream excellent Khao Lam (ข้าวหลาม) (sticky rice and coconut milk cooked in bamboo). The sweet pomelo (ส้มโอหวาน) and fragrant coconut juice (มะพร้าวน้ำหอม) are also notable.

spots.name: Ratchaphreuk
spots.desc: Recognisable by its plastic table and chairs in a comfortable beer garden. Occasional karaoke. The food is good traditional Thai, but you will be tested on your knowledge of Thai cuisine as there is no English menu.

spots.name: Namtok Pa La-u
spots.local: น้ำตกป่าละอู
spots.desc: An 11-tier scenic waterfall in a perennial forest in Kaeng Krachan National Park. Visitors can take a songthaew from Hua Hin to this waterfall. The best time to visit is from Nov-Apr. Camping in the park is permitted, and a tent can be rented at 250 baht per night.

spots.name: Ang Sila
spots.local: (อ่างศิลา
spots.desc: A seaside fishing village. Most villagers are skilled in making implements from granite, mainly mortars and pestles, still widely used in Thai households, and figurines of animals.

spots.name: Khao Sam Muk
spots.local: เขาสามมุข
spots.desc: A low hillock situated between Ang Sila and Bang Saen Beach, along the road facing the seashore. A habitat of scores of wild monkeys, the hilltop affords a panoramic view of the Bang Saen Beach.

spots.name: Laem Thaen
spots.local: แหลมแท่น
spots.desc: It is a cape reaching out to the sea where there are pavilions for relaxation and restaurants. People come here to fish the area.

spots.name: Phra Phutthasihing Shrine
spots.local: หอพระพุทธสิหิงค์
spots.desc: The shrine houses a replica of the Phra Phutthasihing cast in silver.

spots.name: Wat Thammanimit
spots.local: วัดธรรมนิมิตต์
spots.desc: Constructed in 1941 and where the Phra Phutthamongkhon Nimit Buddha image resides. It is a concrete Buddha image decorated with mosaic tiles in the Boarding a Boat posture.

spots.name: Wat Yai Inthraram
spots.local: วัดใหญ่อินทราราม
spots.desc: An ancient and significant temple of Chonburi, influenced by the late Ayutthayan architectural style. The ubosot was built with a curved gunwale base and inside displays murals.

spots.name: Wihan Thep Sathit Phra Kitti Chaloem or Nacha Sa Thai Chue Shrine
spots.local: วิหารเทพสถิตพระกิติเฉลิม หรือ ศาลเจ้าหน่าจาซาไท้จื้อ
spots.desc: A Chinese shrine. It is a 4-storey building decorated in extraordinary Chinese architectural style and housing various Chinese deity images.

spots.name: Chonburi Annual Festival
spots.local: งานนมัสการพระพุทธสิหิงค์และงานกาชาดประจำปีจังหวัดชลบุรี
spots.desc: This fair is held about mid-Apr during the Songkran Festival. Phra Phutthasihing, Chonburi’s principal Buddha image, is put in a procession around the city.

spots.name: Chonburi Buffalo Races
spots.local: (งานประเพณีวิ่งควาย
spots.desc: This is a long-established celebration of this most useful animal. A fun-filled event, it is held not only in Chonburi itself, but also in Ban Bueng and Nong Yai Districts. The beasts of burden are dressed outrageously or with admirable creativity by owners, bounded only by their imaginations. Assembled in the courtyard in front of the town hall, the buffaloes partake in racing, or take part in…

spots.name: Ko Phra Sai Wan Lai Festival
spots.local: งานประเพณีก่อพระทรายวันไหล บางแสน
spots.desc: A festival long celebrated by the Saen Suk people. Originally, it was called "Ngan Thambun Wan Lai", a gathering of people from various villages to make merit during the Songkran Festival or the Thai New Year Day, taking place on 16-17 Apr every year. Monks from every temple in Saen Suk sub-district are invited to perform the religious ceremony. There is merit- making, food offering, and a…

spots.name: Ngan Bun Klang Ban and Phanat Nikhom Basketwork Festival
spots.local: งานบุญกลางบ้าน และเครื่องจักสานพนัสนิคม
spots.desc: Traditions that have been passed on for a long period of time by the Phanat Nikhom people. They are organized on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday in the first week of May or the Thai 6th lunar month. The locals will bring food, offer it to the monks, and dedicate the merit to the guardian spirits, enemies from a former life, deceased relatives, as well as to drive out bad things, to ask for rain…

spots.name: Pattaya–Na Kluea Wan Lai Festival and Na Kluea Kong Khao Fair
spots.local: งานประเพณีวันไหล พัทยา- นาเกลือ และงานกองข้าวนาเกลือ
spots.desc: Held from 18-20 Apr every year at Lan Pho Public Park, Na Kluea, and Wat Chai Mongkhon in south Pattaya.

spots.name: Songkran Si Maha Racha Festival and Kong Khao Tradition
spots.local: งานประเพณีสงกรานต์ศรีมหาราชาและงานประเพณีกองข้าว
spots.desc: An ancient Chonburi festival. Si Racha District preserves this tradition and organizes it every year, from 19-21 Apr, to worship the gods who have been protecting them throughout the year. Activities comprise of the procession led by the elderly and various organizations in traditional Thai costume, a worship ceremony, spirit offering ceremony, Kong Khao tradition demonstration, games…

spots.name: Wan Lai Festival
spots.local: ประเพณีวันไหล
spots.desc: A merit-making day for seamen on the Thai New Year during the Songkran Festival, organised during 13-20 Apr every year. There is alms-offering to the monks, the ceremony of pouring water onto the Buddha’s image, sand pagoda making, splashing water, and local games and sports in Chonburi.

spots.name: City Pillar Shrine
spots.local: ศาลหลักเมือง
spots.desc: This shrine was first built of wood. Then it was replaced by a concrete building with Chinese characteristics. The old city pillar used to be in front of the shrine. A new one has been set up with a four-porched shelter.

spots.name: The Shrine of King Taksin the Great
spots.local: ศาลสมเด็จพระเจ้าตากสิน
spots.desc: Folklore says that King Taksin tied his elephant to a tree while leading the troops to Chanthaburi to retrieve the Kingdom of Siam from Burmese occupation. The shrine houses a statue of the king.

spots.name: Dhammarachanusornsatan
spots.local: ธรรมราชานุสรณ์สถาน
spots.desc: At Kaochamao Rayong, shrine buildings house statues such as a statue of Somdej Phra Putthajarn Tho Phromrangsi, the famous Buddhist priest of the Rattanakosin Age, and King Rama V. There is a coin and antiques museum.

spots.name: Wat Ban Don Shadow Play Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์หนังใหญ่วัดบ้านดอน
spots.desc: exhibits 100 Nang Yai shadow-play characters, or Nang Yai, which is a large piece of leather carved and painted into different characters.

spots.name: Phra Chedi Klang Nam
spots.local: พระเจดีย์กลางน้ำ
spots.desc: In the middle of the Rayong River, two km south of downtown near the mouth of the river, there is a pagoda on an island. It is a landmark for the crews sailing in the river to indicate that they are reaching Rayong Province. On the full moon day of the twelfth lunar month, a celebration is held to change the robe covering the pagoda.

spots.name: Sopha Botanical Park
spots.local: สวนพฤกษชาติโสภา
spots.desc: This 32-rai park is lush with many kinds of trees, particularly Thai. In the compound, three traditional Thai houses on stilts, nearly 100 years old, exhibit ceramics from various periods as well as prehistoric pottery from Ban Chiang World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Ko Thalu
spots.local: เกาะทะลุ
spots.desc: The island is a scuba diving site among coral reefs. The island totals an area of 69 rai, and most remains lush forest. While high cliffs occupy the west, white sandy beaches occupy the east and south of the island.

spots.name: Laem Mae Phim
spots.local: แหลมแม่พิมพ์
spots.desc: Without large waves, the beach is nice for swimming. Restaurants and bungalows dot the beach. Laem Mae Phim is 48 km from Rayong town.

spots.name: Supattra Land Orchard
spots.local: สวนสุภัทรา
spots.desc: The orchard is open for the public to view its fruit, durian, rambutan, mango, grape, star fruit, and longan.

spots.name: Namtok Khao Chamao or Namtok Khlong Nam Sai
spots.local: น้ำตกเขาชะเมา หรือน้ำตกคลองน้ำใส
spots.desc: The waterfall cascades down seven levels, stretching for three km. The large pond called Wang Matcha, is a habitat of brook carp.

spots.name: Pha Sawan
spots.local: ผาสวรรค์
spots.desc: The viewpoint is 1.5 km from the national park headquarters.

spots.name: Namtok Khlong Pla Kang
spots.local: น้ำตกคลองปลาก้าง
spots.desc: The waterfall is three km from the headquarters. Ferns and orchids grow well in this lush forest.

spots.name: Namtok Khlong Hin Phoeng
spots.local: น้ำตกคลองหินเพิง
spots.desc: The small waterfall is in Chantaburi Province, ten km from the headquarters. Water runs all year round.

spots.name: Khao Wong
spots.local: เขาวง
spots.desc: Many limestone mountains surround a flat plain. The mountains have a total of 80 caves inside.

spots.name: Krommaluang Chumphon Shrine
spots.local: ศาลสมเด็จกรมหลวงชุมพร
spots.desc: The shrine houses the statue of Krommaluang Chumphonkhetudomsak, founder of Thailand's modern navy.

spots.name: Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Herbal Park
spots.local: สวนสมุนไพรสมเด็จพระเทพรัตนราชสุดาฯ สยามบรมราชกุมารี
spots.desc: The park grows various kinds of herbs and also conducts research.

spots.name: Suphattra Land
spots.desc: Suphattra Land is an 800-acre orchard where fruit lovers can pick durian, rambutan, mangosteen, starfruit, dragonfruit, etc., off the trees, or just enjoy the pleasant surroundings. Fruits are generally full-grown late April to June. A sightseeing train winds its way through the orchards as well.

spots.name: Wat Don
spots.desc: Good value authentic Thai massage by fully trained, qualified masseuses.

spots.name: The Love Club
spots.desc: A stage full of Thai girls dancing in short-shorts and bikini tops alternate with live bands. Whisky and other alcoholic drinks available by the bottle with mixers of your choice. They also have hookah pipes.

spots.name: Mu Ko Chang National Park
spots.desc: National Marine Park including parts of Ko Chang and 46 other islands.

spots.name: War Memorial Monument
spots.desc: A renovation is underway at the memorial site, with a huge building being constructed (Jan 2018).

spots.name: White Sand Beach
spots.desc: By far the busiest as it is the first beach visitors reach when they arrive on the island.

spots.name: Klong Nonsi
spots.desc: Waterfall on the east side of the island. Reachable by foot from the Klong Plu waterfall, 6 km.

spots.name: Klong Plu
spots.local: น้ำตกคลองพลู
spots.desc: The most popular waterfall, and the only one on the west side of the island.

spots.name: Dive Adventure
spots.desc: Five star PADI IDC diving school offers scuba diving, PADI courses and snorkelling trips into Ko Chang National Marine Park.

spots.name: Diving School Ko Chang
spots.desc: Go diving or learn to dive in the beautiful waters of Ko Chang.

spots.name: Tree Top Adventure Park
spots.desc: Rope and harness tree climbing. Fun activities and amazing views from the top of the trees.

spots.name: Madoosika
spots.desc: Latest fashions. Chic, BOHO, gypsy, hippie, maxi dress, party and sun dresses.

spots.name: Apple
spots.local: แอปเปิ้ล บังกะโล
spots.desc: Probably the cheapest restaurant/bar along White Sand Beach. It has a good location in the middle of the beach. Don't expect anything special, just the usual Thai and Italian dishes common at tourist spots. Upstairs there is a small hut where you can chill out with a beer on pillows. Closing times are early, but if you order before closing time you can keep sitting there as long as you want. They…

spots.name: Nong Bua Seafood
spots.desc: If you pass by, you might wonder why this place is busy every night. A family-owned restaurant open for more than 30 years. Thai, Chinese, Western food, and especially fresh seafood.

spots.name: Rock Sand Restaurant
spots.desc: Thai and Western food. Speciality: Taste of Thailand and finger licking good.

spots.name: Jungle Queen Live Music Bar
spots.desc: The house band plays from around 20:00-24:00, and plays music from Rihanna to AC/DC. People come from all over the island for the live music hour, so be sure to stop by when they are on. They also have free pool, and the place doesn't close until 05:00, so it's a good place to take the party after the nightclub and the other bars start closing. Service is good, and the staff are friendly and…

spots.name: Cafe del Sunshine
spots.desc: Thai food and a great selection of Western brunch and lunch dishes. Set in a nicely designed and relaxing building.

spots.name: Rock Sand Resort
spots.desc: Right by the sea with a terrace over the sea to sit and watch the Ko Chang sunsets. Special: Taste of Thailand. Just above and behind the restaurant Rock Sand has rooms for backpackers and flashpackers.

spots.name: Siam Hut
spots.desc: Hosts a large dance party every Friday night in their large outdoor deck on the beach. Happy hour specials on Friday until 23:00

spots.name: Somdej Phra Srinagarindra Park
spots.local: สวนสมเด็จพระศรีนครินทร์
spots.desc: The park's compound includes an ancient pond, called Sra Pangthong. The park includes beautiful flowers and trees, jungle, water park, rock garden, exercise area, and a 69-m-high fountain.

spots.name: The 60th anniversary of Her Majesty the Queen Park
spots.local: สวนเทิดพระเกียรติ ๖๐ พรรษา มหาราชินี
spots.desc: The park includes a botanical garden, pavilion, fountain, viewpoint, and bird sanctuary.

spots.name: Sakon Nakhon Cultural Centre
spots.local: ศูนย์วัฒนธรรมจังหวัดสกลนคร
spots.desc: The centre features tools, belongings, history, and documents of different ethnic groups.

spots.name: Phra That Dum
spots.local: พระธาตุดุม
spots.desc: The lone stupa is built with laterite in the same period as Phra That Narai Jeng Veng, but the stupa is smaller and without a base. The lintel featuring God Vishnu in reclining position is placed on the northern arch. There are carvings depicting gods riding different animals over the Rahu.

spots.name: Archan Man Purithattha Thera Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์บริขารอาจารย์มั่น ภูริทัตตเถระ
spots.desc: The museum houses a bronze statue of Archan Man Purithatto and the glass case that houses his ashes that turned into crystal. The display, including his tools, is placed on a marble altar and his life history is shown nearby.

spots.name: Sapan Khom or Sapan Hin
spots.local: สะพานขอม หรือสะพานหิน
spots.desc: It is considered as an ancient bridge to link Sakon Nakhon and the countryside as this area once was swamp. The present bridge is made from laterite, replacing the old one that was removed for road construction.

spots.name: Phra That Narai Cheng Weng - Phra That Narai Jengveng Stupa
spots.local: ปราสาทพระธาตุนารายณ์เจงเวง
spots.desc: The lone stupa is built from sandstone on a laterite base and carved beautifully. Its lintel features Lord Krisna killing a lion in Bapuan Khmer art. The art appearing on this stupa is quite similar to many other Khmer ruins found in Isan.

spots.name: Phu Phan Rajanivet Palace
spots.local: พระตำหนักภูพานราชนิเวศน์
spots.desc: The palace is the royal residence of the king, queen, and royal family during their missions in northeast Thailand.

spots.name: Phu Phan National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติภูพาน
spots.desc: The park features limestone mountains and different forest such as deciduous dipterocarp forest, jungle rain forest, or mixed deciduous forest. Wildlife found in the park include langur, civet, and slow loris.

spots.name: Phra That Phu Pek
spots.local: พระธาตุภูเพ็ก
spots.desc: this ancient Khmer Ruin was built from sandstone, standing on a laterite base.

spots.name: Tham Seri Thai
spots.local: ถ้ำเสรีไทย
spots.desc: During WWII, Seri Thai used this cave for arms and food storage as it is well camouflaged by lush vegetation.

spots.name: Phu Phan Mountain Range
spots.local: เทือกเขาภูพาน
spots.desc: The range is quite well known, but remote, at the border of Sakon Nakhon and Kalasin.

spots.name: Namtok Kham Hom and Kong Ping Ngu
spots.local: น้ำตกคำหอม และ โค้งปิ้งงู
spots.desc: The entrance to Namtok Kham Hom winds like a grilled snake, or Kong Ping Ngu in Thai.

spots.name: Pha Nang Mern and Lan Sao E
spots.local: ผานางเมิน และลานสาวเอ้
spots.desc: It is quite a nice place for camping and for watching the sunset view. Below the cliff, there is a track leading to Lan Sao E, literally, "the place for the lady to show beautiful attire".

spots.name: Pha Savoey
spots.local: ผาเสวย
spots.desc: In Kalasin, the cliff heading south is the place where the king once visited and ate lunch.

spots.name: Namtok Huay Yai
spots.local: น้ำตกห้วยใหญ่
spots.desc: The falls are 12 km from park headquarters. It cascades via several steps amid dense jungle.

spots.name: Stone Arch
spots.local: Thang Pi Pan) (สะพานหินธรรมชาติ [ทางผีผ่าน]
spots.desc: The stone arch, 1.5 m wide and 8 m long, bridges two groups of rocks together creating a shelter underneath it.

spots.name: Phu Thai ethnic group at Ban None Hom
spots.local: ชาวภูไท บ้านโนนหอม
spots.desc: have immigrated from the left side of Mekong River to settle down here over a century ago.

spots.name: Cliff carving at Phu Pha Yon
spots.local: ภาพรอยสลักผาสามพันปีที่ภูผายล
spots.desc: Phu Pha Yon, the mountain in the compound of meditation centre houses cliff carvings featuring lifestyles of the local people in the pre-historical period.

spots.name: Wat Tham Kham or Phu Kham
spots.local: วัดถ้ำขาม หรือ ภูขาม
spots.desc: The temple once was a meditation place of Archan Fan Archaro. The temple also houses ashes of Phra Archan Tet Tetrangsi, now a pilgrimage site.

spots.name: Archan Fan Archaro Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์อาจารย์ฝั้น อาจาโร
spots.desc: The museum, in the shape of a pagoda and three folds of lotus, houses a life-size statue of Archan Fan in a sitting posture with a stick in his hand. The other exhibits include ashes in glass box and tools, as well as his history.

spots.name: Wat Kham Pramong
spots.local: วัดคำประมง
spots.desc: This temple served as a meditation place for Phra Kru Santi Worayan (Luang Pu Sim Buddharo).

spots.name: Nam Oun Dam
spots.local: เขื่อนน้ำอูน
spots.desc: The clay dam, managed by the Royal Irrigation Department, is built to preserve water from the Nam Oun, a tributary of the Songkram River which originates in the Phu Phan Range.

spots.name: Prasart Ban Panna
spots.local: ปราสาทบ้านพันนา
spots.desc: The Khmer ruin has a lone stupa with a rectangular laterite base and baray around. It is believed to have been built in the same period as Phra That Phu Pek.

spots.name: Phra That Sri Mongkol
spots.local: พระธาตุศรีมงคล
spots.desc: The rectangular pagoda is decorated in modern design and stucco. Its base contains decorations in terracotta featuring history of Lord Buddha. The modern design is a renovation of the old pagoda which had only a laterite core.

spots.name: Tham Phra Buddha Saiyard
spots.local: Tham Phra Thong or Phu Pha Thong) (ถ้ำพระพุทธไสยาสน์ [ถ้ำพระทอง หรือภูผาทอง]
spots.desc: The cave is at Tambon Kor Kiew, 9 km from Amphoe Warich Phume.

spots.name: Phu Ang Sor
spots.local: ภูอ่างศอ
spots.desc: The mountain is in Tambon Kham Bor, 18 km from Amphoe Warichaphum

spots.name: Wat Tham Apai Damrong Tham or Wat Tham Phuang and the Museum of Archan Wan Uttamo
spots.local: วัดถ้ำอภัยดำรงธรรม หรือวัดถ้ำพวง และพิพิธภัณฑ์อาจารย์วัน อุตตโม
spots.desc: The temple has a four-gabled marble pavilion with a double roof. Its ground floor features paintings of the history of the famous monk Archan Wan.

spots.name: Phu Pha Lek National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติภูผาเหล็ก
spots.desc: The park encloses part of the Phu Phan Range with Phu Ang Sor as its highest peak. Most areas are covered with deciduous dipterocarp forest, mixed dipterocarp forest, dry evergreen forest, various kinds of bamboo and herbs. Wild hogs, barking deer, mouse deer and various birds are found. Attractions in the park include:

spots.name: Pha Suriyan
spots.local: ผาสุริยันต์
spots.desc: The towering cliff on the top of Phu Pha Lek offers nice view point and sun rise view.

spots.name: Pha Dong Kor
spots.local: ผาดงก่อ
spots.desc: The cliff is on the peak of Phu Pha Lek, part of Phu Phan range. It is special with a huge rock at the cliff edge.

spots.name: Pha Nam Joke
spots.local: ผาน้ำโจ้ก
spots.desc: This high cliff on the peak of Phu Pha Lek offers views of Huay Huad Reservoir and a panorama of Udon Thani and Khon Kaen.

spots.name: Pha Pak Wan Pre-historical Painting
spots.local: ภาพเขียนก่อนประวัติศาสตร์ผาผักหวาน
spots.desc: The 3,600-year-old painting is on a big rock at Ban Phu Takham. It features women standing in line and holding each other's shoulders.

spots.name: Lan U-sa Sawan
spots.local: ลานอุษาสวรรค์
spots.desc: The plateau, covering 2.5 km² in area, is on top of Phu Pha Lek. It comprises forest, mountain, rock and grassland, and looks like a man-made garden.

spots.name: Dinosaur graveyard
spots.local: สุสานไดโนเสาร์
spots.desc: Many fossils have been found in the middle of the Phu Pha Lek Mountain and at the forested edge of Phu Phan. Fossils of plant and petrified wood have also been found.

spots.name: Hor Song Dao
spots.local: หอส่องดาว
spots.desc: The observatory is at 700 m elevation on Phu Pha Lek's peak. With a full panoramic view, it is a good place to observe the stars and meteor showers.

spots.name: Nam Phung Dam
spots.local: เขื่อนน้ำพุง
spots.desc: The first rockfill dam in northeast Thailand is 1,720 m long and 40 m high. The dam generates electricity for Sakon Nakhon and Nakhon Phanom.

spots.name: Thai So Cultural Centre
spots.local: ศูนย์วัฒนธรรมไทยโส้
spots.desc: The centre features tools of Thai So, an ethnic group that migrated from the left side of the Mekong River.

spots.name: Phu Pha Yon National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติภูผายล
spots.desc: It features plateau and sandstone mountain, blanketed by deciduous dipterocarp forest, dry evergreen forest, hill evergreen forest. The trees found in the park include thingar, Lagerstroemia calyculata Kurz, Irvingia malayana. Wildlife found includes barking deer, sambar deer, Asiatic wild dog. Attractions in the park include:

spots.name: Huay Huad Reservoir
spots.local: อ่างเก็บน้ำห้วยหวด
spots.desc: It was created by the irrigation dam at the initiative of the king. There is a strangely shaped rock, by the pavilion on the right side of the reservoir.

spots.name: Namtok Kham Sang
spots.local: น้ำตกคำน้ำสร้าง
spots.desc: With a height of 25 m, these are the highest falls in the park. The falls are 1.8 km from park headquarters.

spots.name: Phu Pha Yon
spots.local: ภูผายล
spots.desc: The mountain has beautiful scenery. Its cliff houses carvings which can be dated back to over 3,000 years ago.

spots.name: Pha Paya Tao Ngoy
spots.local: ผาพญาเต่างอย
spots.desc: There is a rock in "ngoy tortoise" shape which is going towards Phung Stream. Locals believe that the tortoise represents fertile land and named the village Ban Tao Ngoy.

spots.name: Lan Dusita
spots.local: ลานดุสิตา
spots.desc: The vast rock plain turns colourful in late rainy season when various tiny flowers are in full bloom.

spots.name: Wax Castle Procession
spots.local: งานประเพณีแห่ปราสาทผึ้ง
spots.desc: Held during the 12th-15th days of the waxing moon in October to mark the end of Buddhist Lent. On the night of 13th day, people join to decorate wax castles at Ming Muang Field. On the 14th day, wax castles from different temples will join the procession, roaming the municipality to Wat Phra That Cherngchum Woravihara. Isan people believe that the wax will welcome Lord Buddha who comes back from…

spots.name: Songkran Festival
spots.desc: Songkran is Thailand's traditional New Years from the 13-15 Apr annually. Do not think Songkran is just for the big cities as seemingly the entire town comes out to play for several days of water throwing madness. It is about the best fun you can have in Sakon. Most of the action takes place from the temple Wat Phra That Choeng Chum and several blocks to the northwest.

spots.name: Big C Shopping Centre
spots.desc: General shopping. There's a food court, a MK Restaurant and a decent sushi stand.

spots.name: Kut Na Kham Arts and Crafts Centre
spots.desc: Where pottery, fabrics, and wood carvings are made by hand to unique designs.

spots.name: Robinson
spots.desc: Groceries and assorted goods, with much higher pricing than Big C or Lotus.

spots.name: Tedsaban Market
spots.desc: Primarily a vegetable market, but you can also buy some cheap clothes (especially at night when the market expands to the opposite side of the street) and other odds-and-ends. It's also a great place to pick up a quick Thai meal in a plastic bag.

spots.name: Ban Fa Prong Coffee & Bakery
spots.desc: Delicious range of Thai, Isaan, French, and international cuisine with menu in English. Air-con, English spoken, nice set of international desserts.

spots.name: Dog Meat
spots.desc: Dog meat is sold to those meat-eaters desperate to taste sour and spicy dog-bone soup, peppery dog meat salad, or dark spicy smoked dog sausage. Gourmets say the meat, boiled or fried, is particularly succulent and tastes like deer. Dog oil is said claimed to be a useful ointment for scratches or burned skin. The thought of eating dog horrifies most Thais, and the promotion of canine cuisine is…

spots.name: Green Corner
spots.desc: A modern bakery and restaurant. Sells Thai and Western meals. Popular with expats and foreigners also because it's one of the few restaurants that has an English language menu and air-con.

spots.name: Pon Yang Kham
spots.desc: A butchery specialising in the production and distribution of high quality beef from charolais and limousin French cattle breeds. Supplies high-end restaurants in Bangkok. Also has an affordable restaurant at noon.

spots.name: Sakon Nakhon Farmers Market (AKA bypass market)
spots.desc: Fruits, vegetables, mushrooms, meat, fish, takeaway food, and an amazing range of insects, frogs, birds, snakes, larvae, worms.

spots.name: Patchachin
spots.desc: Thai pub and restaurant. Very popular with younger affluent Thais. No English language menus.

spots.name: Soi Jet
spots.desc: Hard to find but serves good quality Thai food. It is another pub popular with younger, affluent Thais looking for a more relaxed night out. Thai-language menu only.

spots.name: Ancient Kiln Sites
spots.local: แหล่งเตาโบราณ
spots.desc: The kilns date from around the 9th–10th centuries and served as a production centre for Khmer ceramics supplying other cities.

spots.name: Big Buddha Image
spots.local: พระพุทธรูปใหญ่
spots.desc: Or Phra Phuttharup Patima Santayaphirom Satuek Udom Ratsadon Nimitmanin is a big standing Buddha image on a bank of the Mun River.

spots.name: Huai Talat Reservoir and Buriram Bird Park
spots.local: อ่างเก็บน้ำห้วยตลาดและสวนนกบุรีรัมย์
spots.desc: More than 100 species of birds live in this area during the dry season, Nov-Apr.

spots.name: Khao Kradong Forest Park
spots.local: วนอุทยานเขากระโดง
spots.desc: This extinct volcano is now a relaxation spot. The summit is 265 m above sea level and it houses "Phra Suphattharabophit", a large Buddha image that is the symbol of Buriram.

spots.name: Kradong Reservoir
spots.desc: From the entrance to Khao Kradong, there is a junction on the left side to "Bunyanusat" boy scout camp and a zoo.
spots.addr: อ่างเก็บน้ำกระโดง

spots.name: Ku Suan Taeng
spots.local: กู่สวนแตง
spots.desc: A Khmer architectural site, comprising three brick prangs lying from north to south, on the same laterite base.

spots.name: Lam Nang Rong Dam
spots.local: เขื่อนลำนางรอง
spots.desc: A royal project, the Lam Nang Rong Dam is an earthen dam with an asphalt road along the crest with an expansive view.

spots.name: Lower Northeastern Cultural Centre
spots.local: ศูนย์วัฒนธรรมอีสานใต้
spots.desc: The centre collects and exhibits artefacts and precious historical objects, folk art, and archaeological curiosities. It is also a resource centre for conducting research.

spots.name: King Rama I Monument
spots.local: พระบรมราชานุสาวรีย์พระบาทสมเด็จพระพุทธยอดฟ้าจุฬาโลก
spots.desc: The monument was built in 1996 to honour King Rama I who founded Buriram.

spots.name: Prasat Nong Hong
spots.local: ปราสาทหนองหงส์
spots.desc: A small archaeological site comprising three prangs made from brick on a single laterite base.

spots.name: Prasat Wat Khok Ngio
spots.local: ปราสาทวัดโคกงิ้ว
spots.desc: A Khmer stone sanctuary behind Wat Khok Ngio, and it once served as an "Arogayasala" or a hospital.

spots.name: Phrachao Yai Wat Hong
spots.local: พระเจ้าใหญ่วัดหงษ์
spots.desc: An old Lao-style Buddha image in the posture of subduing Mara, which was built during the late Ayutthaya period, or around the 18th century.

spots.name: Rao Su Monument
spots.local: อนุสาวรีย์เราสู้
spots.desc: Built in 1979 to commemorate the brave undertakings of civilians, police officers, and soldiers who lost their lives during battles with communists who obstructed the construction of this strategic route.

spots.name: Silk Weaving Village of Na Pho
spots.local: หมู่บ้านทอผ้าไหมอำเภอนาพธิ์
spots.desc: A silk weaving village, famed for "Mudmi" silk, which has received support for their skills, the standard of production, and their patterns and colours from the Royal Folk Arts and Craft Centre under the royal patronage of Queen Sirikit.

spots.name: Stone Quarry
spots.local: แหล่งหินตัด
spots.desc: The quarry was used by the ancient Khmer people as a source of construction materials for building sanctuaries in the lower northeastern region.

spots.name: Thung Laem Reservoir
spots.local: อ่างเก็บน้ำทุ่งแหลม
spots.desc: A small reservoir which has been transformed into a recreational site with shelters for rest and relaxation. During the dry season, many species of waterfowl can be found here.

spots.name: Wat Khao Angkhan
spots.local: วัดเขาอังคาร
spots.desc: Inside the temple compound, there are ruins of ancient monuments and sandstone boundary markers of the Dvaravati period. It is one of the most beautiful and significant temples in Buriram.

spots.name: Buriram United
spots.desc: Buriram is well-known for its great local football club. They play in the new I-Mobile Stadium.

spots.name: Sro Ground
spots.desc: Walking Street is a popular attraction on Saturday and Sunday evenings. The sign at the intersection of Jira Rd and Romburi Rd translates to Walking Street but it is known by the locals as "Sro Ground" or the "River Market" as it is next to a part of the moat. The market has around a hundred stalls selling items such as clothes, footwear, inexpensive jewellery and glassware. Approximately half of…

spots.name: Baan Chay Nam Restaurant
spots.local: ร้านอาหารบ้านชายน้ำ
spots.desc: Excellent. Very popular, live music, sit in or outside at the back near the fountain.

spots.name: Muang Buri Ram Municipal Night Bazaar
spots.local: ร้านอาหารบ้านชายน้ำ
spots.desc: A really nice night market with the usual Thai snacks like fried pork sausage, fried chicken, mango sticky rice & Thai sweets; But also tiny back-alley makeshift restaurants that serve a wide variety of dishes, like laab moo, khao soy gai and spicy northern–style sausages.

spots.name: The Square
spots.desc: Karaoke bars, restaurants, and the huge Speed1 nightclub featuring live shows and a DJ playing Thai and Western hits every night.

spots.name: Thung Si Muang Park
spots.local: ทุ่งศรีเมือง
spots.desc: At the centre of town in front of city hall, this pleasant little park has several points of interest. A bright yellow elaborately carved candle sculpture, completed in 2000, standing 22 m tall and dedicated to the king, showcases Isaan art styles and has become the symbol of the city. The candle is placed on a junk, with a garuda eagle at the bow and a naga serpent around it. A statue of Phra…

spots.name: Prasat Ban Ben
spots.local: ปราสาทบ้านเบญจ์
spots.desc: The Khmer sanctuary is a religious site comprising three brick prangs on separated laterite bases. The Fine Arts Department excavated the site in 1990 and found lintels featuring nine directional guardian angels and the God Indra on his Erawan heavenly elephant.

spots.name: Hat Khu Duea
spots.local: หาดคูเดื่อ
spots.desc: This beach on the Mun River is 12 km from downtown Ubon Ratchathani via Highway 24.

spots.name: Sirindhorn Dam
spots.local: เขื่อนสิรินธร
spots.desc: Called Khuean Dom Noi by the people of the area, the rockfill dam with a clay core was constructed across the Lam Dom Noi, a tributary of the Mun River. The hydroelectric dam is 42 metres high and 940 metres long.

spots.name: Ban Kan Lueang Archaeological Site
spots.local: แหล่งโบราณคดีบ้านก้านเหลือง
spots.desc: An archaeological site which can be dated back to 2,800-2,500 years ago. In 1996, the Fine Arts Department found a number of artefacts such as beads, pottery, bronze bells, iron axes, and chaff.

spots.name: Ban Pa-ao
spots.local: บ้านปะอาว
spots.desc: This ancient village is in Tambon Nong Khon. Two centuries ago, the villagers immigrated from Vientiane during the reign of King Siri Bunsan. The village produces brass work in an ancient style.

spots.name: Annamese Lion Pulpit at Ban Chi Thuan
spots.local: ธรรมาสน์สิงห์ศิลปะญวนที่บ้านชีทวน
spots.desc: The Buddhist pulpit is placed at Wat Sinuan Saeng Sawang Arom. The concrete pulpit itself is unique, with a lion sculpture carrying the pulpit with decorative stucco, multi-layer wooden roof, and painting in the Annamese style.

spots.name: Sao Chaliang
spots.local: เสาเฉลียง
spots.desc: Carved by wind and water for millions of years, the mushroom-like stone towers are scattered around the area containing shell fossils, sand and gravels in their texture. Geologists think that over a million years ago this area was a sea.

spots.name: Namtok Soi Sawan
spots.local: น้ำตกสร้อยสวรรค์
spots.desc: Two streams, Huai Soi and Huai Phai, combine and plunge 20 metres down to the pond below, making the waterfall look like a necklace – "soi" in Thai.

spots.name: Namtok Saeng Chan or Namtok Ru
spots.local: น้ำตกแสงจันทร์หรือ น้ำตกรู
spots.desc: The tiny cascade is special as the stream falls through a hole, "ru", down to the pond below. At noon, sunshine through the hole makes the waterfall look like a ray of moonshine, "saeng chan".

spots.name: Dong Na Tham Forest
spots.local: ป่าดงนาทาม
spots.desc: From September to November is the best time to visit as flowers are in full bloom. There are waterfalls and fogs over the Mekong River. From January to March the forest changes its hue, with trees shedding their leaves, and cruises in the Mekong run from Ban Pak La to Khan Tha Kwian.

spots.name: Namtok Huai Sai Yai or Kaeng I Khiao
spots.local: น้ำตกห้วยทรายใหญ่ หรือ แก่งอีเขียว
spots.desc: The waterfall is in the Buntharik–Khao Yot Mon Wildlife Sanctuary. The waterfall runs over the rock terrace in a shady environment.

spots.name: Phu Chong Na Yoi National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติภูจอง-นายอย
spots.desc: The park covers a total area of 686 km2. Its boundary connects to Laos and Cambodia in the area called the Emerald Triangle.
spots.price: For Thai people: 10 baht for children, 20 baht for adults. For foreigners: 100 baht for children, 200 baht for adults.…

spots.name: Kaeng Tana National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติแก่งตะนะ
spots.desc: The park features plateaus and undulating hills with deciduous dipterocarp forest and grassland.
spots.price: For Thai people: 10 baht for children, 20 baht for adults. For foreigners: 100 baht for children, 200 baht for adults.…

spots.name: Wat Nong Bua
spots.desc: A very unusual large white angular chedi, said to be a copy of the Mahabodhi stupa in Bodh Gaya, India. Quite stunning in appearance, but the decorations seem rather modern and with reason. The structure was built only in 1957 to commemorate the 2500th anniversary of Buddha's death.

spots.name: Wat Nong Pah Pong
spots.local: วัดหนองป่าพง
spots.desc: The forest monastery of the late venerable Ajahn Chah, who is one of the most famous meditation masters in Thailand. About 70 monks live here, including some foreign ones, and there is a small museum and a stupa (or chedi) with the relics of Ajahn Chah to visit. The temple is in a lush forest of Tambon Non Phueng. Monks study and practice Vipassana meditation there. The temple has the Phra…

spots.name: Wat Pah Nanachat
spots.local: International Forest Monastery วัดป่านานาชาติ
spots.desc: A famous forest meditation temple with more than 20 foreign/Western monks from all over the world. If you come before 08:00 you can join in the morning meal, and maybe speak to a monk afterwards. You can take a red songthaew from Warin Chamrab to Wat Pah Nanachat for about 10 baht. Numerous foreign monks study and practice Vipassana meditation here; most of them can speak Thai fluently and pray…

spots.name: Wat Thung Si Muang
spots.local: วัดทุ่งศรีเมือง
spots.desc: Primarily notable for its wooden scripture hall (hor trai), on stilts above a pond. The monastery was built in the reign of Rama III (1824-51) to house a replica of Buddha's footprint. The Buddha's footprint is housed in the ubosot which mirrors art blending between the early Rattanakosin era and that of Vientiane. Another important building in the temple is the Ho Trai, the Hall of Tipitaka…

spots.name: Wat Si Ubon Rattanaram or Wat Si Thong
spots.local: วัดศรีอุบลรัตนาราม หรือ วัดศรีทอง
spots.desc: The ubosot houses a sacred Buddha image known as “Phra Kaeo Butsarakham”. The Buddha image, in the attitude of subduing Mara, is carved from topaz into the Chiang Saen style. Each year, in the Songkran Festival, people parade the Buddha image for the people to pay their respects to and bathe.

spots.name: Wat Chaeng
spots.local: วัดแจ้ง
spots.desc: The ubosot, which was only completed 24 years later, is noted for its architecture and rare woodcarving. As a heritage site, the ubosot is well preserved in its original condition. It won a Certificate of Honour from Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn in the "Architect 87" Exhibition.

spots.name: Wat Maha Wanaram
spots.local: วัดมหาวนาราม
spots.desc: It was at first only a "Samnak Song", a monastic residence, for Vipassana monks. According to a stone inscription found behind the principal Buddha statue, Phrachao Yai In Paeng, it was built in 1807. The stucco Buddha statue, in the attitude of subduing Mara, was built in the Laotian style.

spots.name: Wat Burapharam
spots.local: วัดบูรพาราม
spots.desc: The temple once served as a residence for famous meditation monks. Today, the temple houses lifelike stone figures of these monks.

spots.name: Wat Supattanaram Worawihan
spots.local: วัดสุปัฏนารามวรวิหาร
spots.desc: This is the first Dhammayutika temple of the province. The temple has a special ubosot designed by a royal highway engineer Luang Sathit Nimankan (Chuan Supiyaphan). It has a Thai-style roof, Western-style hall and Khmer-style base.

spots.name: Wat Phukhao Kaeo
spots.local: วัดภูเขาแก้ว
spots.desc: The temple has an ubosot delicately decorated with a tiered roof covered with terracotta tiles and supporting a golden spire in the middle. Inside is a high-relief regarding important phrathats, relic-containing pagodas, of Thailand.

spots.name: Wat Thung Si Wilai
spots.local: วัดทุ่งศรีวิไล
spots.desc: The temple houses Luangpho Wiset, the principal Buddha image carved from laterite seated beneath the Naga's hood. The Buddha image from the Dvaravati period is considered a sacred icon for the village. The temple is surrounded by several enclosures of Sima stones that mark the temple’s consecrated boundary.

spots.name: Wat Tham Kuha Sawan
spots.local: วัดถ้ำคูหาสวรรค์
spots.desc: The temple was built by Luangpu Khamkhaning Chulamani to be a place for meditation practice where he also resided. After Luangpu's death his body, which did not decompose, was put in a glass coffin and is considered sacred.

spots.name: Candle Festival
spots.local: งานประเพณีแห่เทียนเข้าพรรรษา
spots.desc: Ubon's biggest event. Held in early-July on Khao Phansa day, which marks the beginning of the rainy season retreat. For three months, monks do not leave their temple except for an emergencies, and laypersons vow to abstain from drinking alcohol as well as bonking. Huge wax candles are displayed in Thung Si Muang Park, which are carried around town in a procession the next morning.

spots.name: Illuminated Boat Procession
spots.local: งานประเพณีไหลเรือไฟ
spots.desc: This less well-known festival is held in October on the river near the Rattanakosin Bicentennial Bridge to mark the end of the rainy season (Ok Phansa).

spots.name: Flower Festival
spots.local: งานเทศกาลไม้ดอกไม้ประดับ
spots.desc: Held every February at Thung Kham Nam Saep Stadium, Amphoe Warin Chamrap, the festival features floral floats, decorative and flowering plant contests, and fair.

spots.name: Kaeng Saphue Songkran Festival
spots.local: งานประเพณีมหาสงกรานต์แก่งสะพือ
spots.desc: Held every April in Amphoe Phibun Mangsahan, the festival includes a beauty contest, fair, local sports, and local music contest.

spots.name: Traditional Boat Races
spots.local: งานแข่งขันเรือยาวประเพณี
spots.desc: Several boat racing tournaments are held annually in October after the end of Buddhist Lent. The Mueang Ubon Ratchathani Municipality's tournament is held near the Rattanakosin Bicentennial Bridge. Tambon Phibun Mangsahan Municipality's tournament is held near the Mun River Bridge, and Wat Pho Tak's tournament is held in front of the temple.

spots.name: Phanchat Esan Folk Arts & Handicrafts
spots.desc: Wide selection of souvenirs and handicrafts. Has two beautifully designed locations downtown.

spots.name: 126 Cafe Ubon
spots.desc: A secret cafe with live acoustic music. Provided healthy drinks made from soy milk and delicious fusion cuisines

spots.name: Muen Thip
spots.desc: A popular two-storey place specializing in a Thai interpretation of Korean barbecue (Neua Yang Kaolee), grilled at your own table and dipped in fiery sauces. A plate of your meat of choice and a large tray of veggies, plenty for two, costs 90 baht. English menu available, not that you really need it.

spots.name: The Outside Inn
spots.desc: Variety of cuisine- authentic, made-from-scratch Mexican food, Thai classics, Isaan and Lao specialties, and Western favourites. Many offered in vegetarian and vegan versions. Menu isn’t huge, but it’s varied and unique.

spots.name: Peppers Restaurant & Bakery
spots.desc: Great Western and Thai food, along with coffee cakes, pies, fruit shakes, milkshakes, tea, cocktails, beer and wine.

spots.name: Spago Original Italian Pizza
spots.desc: The pizzas are baked in a wood-fired oven and the flour and tomatoes are imported from Italy.

spots.name: Xero Coffee Club
spots.desc: 2-floor co-work space and coffee house, opened in October 2018. It’s American-owned, the coffee is fresh, there are an assortment of homemade cake loaves including banana bread. Unusually for Ubon Ratchathani, you can also create your own sandwich. Nice owner and fast, kind service.

spots.name: Wat Si Chum
spots.local: Thai: วัดศรีชุม
spots.desc: Wat Si Chum complex is north west of the central zone and south west of Wat Phra Phai Luang. It is known for its giant Buddha statue known as Phra Achana (Buddha who is not afraid) and Phra Poot Dai (speaking Buddha).

spots.name: Wat Tham Hip Bon
spots.desc: Located on a quiet shaddy hilltop of about 200 m high, Wat Tham Hip Bon comprises two chedi flanking a modestly sized viharn (assembly hall). The remains of a smaller assembly hall and a few other structures are scattered about the site.

spots.name: Wat Pa Mamuang
spots.local: Thai: วัดป่ามะม่วง
spots.desc: Located slightly north of the road leading out of the Or Gate (West Gate) this shrine consists of the remains of building in the temple include the ordination hall and chedis (stupa).

spots.name: Wat Wihan Thong
spots.desc: Wat Wihan Thong is 1.6 km southeast of the South Gate (Namo Gate). A lotus bud shaped chedi dominates the ruined complex.

spots.name: Wat Chedi Sung
spots.desc: Wat Chedi Sung is 1.2 km east of the East Gate (Kamphaeng Hak Gate) and is about 200 m south of the main road. It houses the second tallest chedi in entire Sukhothai (only Wat Mahatat is higher) but the free-standing chedi seems to look taller.

spots.name: Phra Mae Ya Shrine
spots.local: ศาลพระแม่ย่า
spots.desc: The shrine is highly respected by Sukhothai residents. It houses an idol of Phra Mae Ya, a stone figure with a long face, tapered chin, long halo and dressed as an ancient queen. The idol is supposed to have been built during King Ramkhamhaeng the Great's reign as a dedication to his late mother Nang Sueang. In this connection, the word Phra Mae Ya or grandmother in Thai is literally a term of…

spots.name: Fish Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์ปลาในวรรณคดีเฉลิมพระเกียรติ
spots.desc: It displays a variety of fresh water fish mentioned in Thai literature, such as the travel poems titled Kap Ho Khlong Nirat Phra Bat and Kap Ho Khlong Praphat Than Thongdaeng, and the Kap He Ruea boat song by Chaofa Thammathibet (Chaofa Kung).

spots.name: Sawankhaworanayok National Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติสวรรควรนายก
spots.desc: Houses exhibits in a two-storey building. Upstairs houses sculptural collections from various periods, mostly those formerly collected within the compound of Wat Sawankharam and offered by Phra Sawankhaworanayok. In addition, there are Buddha images, relocated from the Ramkhamhaeng National Museum, from the pre-Sukhothai to the early Ayutthaya period.

spots.name: Centre for Study and Preservation of Sangkhalok Kilns
spots.local: ศูนย์ศึกษาและอนุรักษ์เตาสังคโลก (เตาทุเรียง)
spots.desc: Once the industrial area of Si Satchanalai. Numerous celadon wares in broken, as well as perfect, condition have been discovered. The kiln is oval in shape with a curved roof like that of a ferryboat and is 7–8 m long. The centre consists of two buildings situated on the kiln site area with two kilns Nos. 42 (ground level) and 61 (underground) exhibited in situ. There are also exhibitions on…

spots.name: Sangkhalok Museum
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์สังคโลกสุโขทัย
spots.desc: The museum displays more than 2,000 pieces of Sangkhalok ceramic wares collected from various local and international sources.

spots.name: The Holy Heart Land
spots.desc: An apparently artificial heart-shaped island inside a heart-shaped water basin (from birds-eye view), with a shrine in the center.

spots.name: A Buddha figure
spots.desc: Available in all historic styles, sizes, and materials. It's forbidden to export Buddha figures from Thailand, even though it is commonly done.

spots.name: Thongchai Wittayu
spots.desc: A large electronics shop with good prices for digital cameras, memory cards, MP3s, etc.

spots.name: Ban Kru Eiw
spots.desc: One of Sukhothai's noodle restaurants. Not only Sukhothai noodles, but also Sukhothai-style pad Thai, Vietnamese food, desserts. The restaurant is only open in the daytime which mainly serves for brunch and lunch.

spots.name: Chopper Bar
spots.desc: A rooftop restaurant and bar with good service, live acoustic guitar music, and Thai and Western menus.

spots.name: Dream Café
spots.desc: In a charming rustic old Thai house, serves up a good selection of Thai and Western dishes. Attentive service, eclectic music, and charming decor. There is also a small guesthouse at the back. Chat with the owner Chabah if she's there. She is a genuine renaissance woman, Thai-style.

spots.name: Fueng Fah
spots.desc: Mainly serves dinner. Also a drinking spot where you can enjoy sipping beer by the Yom River. The food is called "fish food". Sukhothai local fish (bla) dishes.

spots.name: Poo Restaurant
spots.desc: This is a Belgian-run restaurant offering Thai and Western food and a wide selection of cocktails.

spots.name: Sukhothai Night Market
spots.desc: Varieties of local food stalls. The night market is called "to-rung". It encompasses the food stalls along the Rachathani temple's fence.

spots.name: Ban Sao Nak (Thai: บ้านเสานัก)
spots.desc: An old teak house, Lanna-style with 116 pillars, more than 105 years old. Serves as a museum.

spots.name: Chae Son National Park
spots.local: อุทยานแห่งชาติแจ้ซ้อน
spots.desc: It is surrounded by a mineral hot spring and rocks. There are many interesting places that are located at Chae Son National Park; for instance, hot spring, Chae Son waterfall, Mae Mon waterfall, Pha-Ngam cave. The most popular place for tourists is Chae Son hot spring where you can cook eggs in 15 minutes. It has a special menu at Chae Son hot spring called "spicy egg salad by mineral hot…

spots.name: Dhanabadee Ceramic Museum
spots.desc: This museum shows the origin of the local specialism of “chicken ceramic bowl”, and demonstrates their production. The aim of this museum is to conserve the local culture and support those who are interested in ceramics.

spots.name: Houses in the old town
spots.desc: The old market street runs parallel to the river. This was the business centre of the town. Today you can see houses in the Burmese Lanna style and Chinese businessmen's houses with wooden doors and delicately carved windows.

spots.name: Thai Elephant Conservation Center
spots.local: ศูนย์อนุรักษ์ช้างไทย
spots.desc: The proceeds from this government-run centre go toward research and elephant conservation initiatives. The center is home to about 50 domesticated elephants, including the first elephant born from artificial insemination, and six of the 10 royal white elephants. The center hosts three daily elephant shows (200 baht for adults, 100 baht for children) at 10:00, 11:00, and 13:00, lasting about 30-45…

spots.name: Wat Pha Fang
spots.local: วัดป่าฝาง
spots.desc: Temple erected in the 19th century with a golden chedi containing reliquaries brought here from Burma. Built during the reign of King Rama IV by Burmese, Wat Pa Fang has a large, glittering gold chedi containing a holy relic brought from Burma around 1906. The extensive Sala Kan Parian (preaching hall) is made entirely of wood with Burmese-style overlapping roofs. Almost across Wat Pa Fang is Wat…

spots.name: Wat Phra Kaew Don Tao
spots.local: วัดพระแก้วดอนเต้า
spots.desc: It used to be the place where the Emerald Buddha was once enshrined (the statue is now installed in Bangkok). Interesting structures include the large chedi containing the hair of the Lord Buddha, a Burmese-style mondop, an ancient viharn and a museum exhibiting ancient relics of the Lanna era.

spots.name: Wat Si Chum
spots.desc: The temple has a small ceremonial hall in Burmese-style. The temple is the seat of a small community of monks from Burma.

spots.name: Wat Si Rong Mueang
spots.local: วัดศรีรองเมือง
spots.desc: A temple erected in Burmese-style in 1905 when the teak wood trade flourished and Burmese traders came into the town. Major architectural works include the viharn made of wood with several overlapping gables in the Burmese style.

spots.name: Wat Chedi Sao Lang
spots.local: วัดเจดีย์ซาวหลัง
spots.desc: The temple has 20 white chedis and a statue of Buddha in Burmese-style. Cool and shaded by large trees, the temple has 20 chedis in its compound, each made in the combined Lanna-Burmese style. A Chiang Saen-style bronze Buddha statue is also enshrined here, commonly referred to as "Phra Chao Than Chai" by the local people.

spots.name: Wat Phrathat Chom Ping
spots.local: วัดพระธาตุจอมปิง
spots.desc: The amazing aspect of this temple is the natural-coloured reflection of the phrathat passing through the hole of the window and appearing on the floor inside the Phra ubosot all the time when there is light, both during the day and at night.

spots.name: Wat Phrathat Lampang Luang
spots.local: วัดพระธาตุลำปางหลวง
spots.desc: Traditional Lanna architecture on the site of ancient Lampang city is famous for murals from the 19th century. The city seal features a white cockerel in the temple's gate. A paradigm of temple building of Lanna. The temple itself is prominently sited on a hillock surrounded by walls. The entrance arches, called Pratu Khong (ประตูโขง), is adorned with fine plaster designs. The wall-less main…

spots.name: Khantok Chang Fair
spots.local: งานขันโตกช้าง หรือ สะโตกช้าง
spots.desc: First Friday and Saturday in February. Elephants are fed with fruits and vegetables on the traditional Lanna Tok tablet. There is an elephant show and the pachyderms are feasted with their popular fruits and vegetables which are placed on the tok, a traditional food tray of the Lanna people.

spots.name: Luang Wiang Lakhon Fair
spots.local: งานหลวงเวียงละคอน
spots.desc: Festival related to the history of the city, local customs and traditions. It is held just prior to the annual Loy Krathong featuring Lampang's historical background and long-established customs and traditions. A Khrua Than procession is organized with local people dressed in native attires carrying various traditional household appliances, some of which are of ancient vintage.
spots.hours: End of October, beginning of November
spots.addr: Wat Phra Keao Don Tao and Wat Phra Thta Lampang Luang

spots.name: Sangchai Outlet
spots.desc: Lampang is a major ceramics centre of Thailand. Up and down Hwy 11 you will find ceramics factories with outlets. An especially good one is Sangchai, which sells a wide range of pottery with the chicken motif along with local goodies such as khao tan biscuits. It's common to see out-of-town Thais shopping for souvenirs.

spots.name: Wood carvings
spots.local: ไม้แกะสลัก
spots.desc: Wood-carving () is a major industry at Tambon Na Khrua of Mae Tha District. Most local people make their living by producing wooden figures of animals in various sizes. It has been a cottage industry in this locality for generations.

spots.name: Sa paper
spots.local: กระดาษสา
spots.desc: A product made from a type of soft wood. The process is purely traditional and the major producing center is the village of Ban Nam Thong. The Sa is mainly made into parasols, lampshades, decorative flowers and other souvenir items.

spots.name: Ka-nom Thai Maipanom
spots.desc: Legend of Thailand local dessert. You can find any kind of Thai dessert here. Beware! If you buy some desserts that contain some coconut milk, you need to put it in the refrigerator to keep them last longer.

spots.name: Kad Tung Kwian Market
spots.desc: Souvenirs, local food, local products, wild food and many more things are available here. This is one of the best markets that you can find in the north of Thailand.

spots.name: Aroy One Baht
spots.desc: Excellent, mainly visited by locals but definitely advisable for tourists.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: Many assorted cheap food stalls with tables and seating. On the left at the market entrance is a 7-Eleven that sells (and opens) beer bottles and soft drinks to go with your meal.

spots.name: Kin Dee
spots.desc: Ranging from Thailand’s local dishes to international dishes, is all available here. Very tasty food, clean and reasonable price.

spots.name: Introvert
spots.desc: Modern style cafe. Get some refreshing drinks for beginning the fresh new day. Not only delicious drinks, you can also find some lovely desserts or even breakfast and lunch. Highly recommended to taste by yourself, and you will love it forever.

spots.name: RPM Red Power Motor
spots.desc: A well-known motorbike rental shop in Mae Haad. They almost always have 125 cc Honda Clicks with dirt tires available, which are more than capable of getting you anywhere on the island with some patience. Proper dirt bikes are frequently available also, though these are overkill unless it's the rainy season.

spots.name: Alvaro Diving Koh Tao
spots.desc: Small family-run dive and freedive shop with new equipment, flexible boat schedules and friendly multilingual staff. Teach PADI & SSI diving and SSI freediving courses in small groups in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere.

spots.name: Apnea Total
spots.desc: Ko Tao's first and longest established freediving school. Apnea Total profits from experienced teachers and a private boat for a safe and successful learning experience.

spots.name: Blue Immersion Freediving
spots.desc: Freedive off Sairee Beach by longtail boat with accomplished instructor Akim. AIDA and SSI courses available.

spots.name: Asia Divers Resort
spots.desc: 5-star Gold PADI Instructor Development Centre offers a full range of diving courses, including divemaster internships. Multiple languages. The resort's bar is always a nice place to chill out after diving.

spots.name: Ban's Diving Resort
spots.desc: PADI open water courses up to professional PADI Instructor courses. A full range of technical diving courses.

spots.name: Big Blue Diving Resort
spots.desc: PADI dive resort with beach side bar and restaurant, lodging with more than 50 rooms. Offers all courses from beginner to instructor, all technical diving. Also offers eco-internships. Winner of PADI's Project Aware Environmental Achievement Award. One of the longest established dive centres on Ko Tao.

spots.name: Big Bubble Dive Resort
spots.desc: One of the long-established dive centres on Ko Tao. Relaxed, fun diving. Scuba diving lessons from beginner to PADI divemaster training with a well trained, professional staff. Also in Chalok Baan Kao.

spots.name: Buddha View IDC Dive Resort
spots.desc: PADI 5-star IDC gold palm resort with friendly staff, good facilities and a BBQ and beach bar to relax in the evenings. Dive instructor courses and professional training programmes with a divemaster.

spots.name: Calypso Diving Koh Tao
spots.desc: Dive training (hands on, no video teaching) from beginner to pro following CMAS and PADI standards in small groups. Located in quiet and party-free bay with a house reef in front of the premises.

spots.name: Coral Grand Divers Resort
spots.desc: Hotel is more up-market and better suited for families. Operates 2 dive boats plus a speed boat.

spots.name: Crystal Dive Resort
spots.desc: PADI scuba diving resort. All PADI dive courses, scuba internships and pro level divemaster and instructor courses. Free accommodation.

spots.name: Davy Jones Locker
spots.desc: PADI open water courses, divemaster internships and PADI instructor training, and MCA boat handling courses in their RIB. Accommodation and gear packages are available for all courses.

spots.name: Dive Point
spots.desc: PADI 5-star dive shop run by an Austrian. Offering diving classes in German, French, Italian, and English. Small groups and individual care for students special needs.

spots.name: Go Pro Diving
spots.desc: Concentrates on PADI Go Pro courses on Ko Tao. PADI divemaster course, IDC course, IDC staff instructor course and master instructor training with full dive internship programs are available.

spots.name: Impian Divers 5 Star Dive Center
spots.desc: Groups limited to 4 divers per pro dive leader. Courses in 5 languages. European-owned/managed with strong safety record/procedures, but still easy going. Differ from most dive centres because of the daily different locations for the dive trips, long dive times. and non-early morning departures. 12 years of experience diving around Ko Tao.

spots.name: Island Dive Club
spots.desc: Does good deals on course and accommodation packages. The Thai staff can be annoying, so deal with the foreigners, they really make the effort. The dive shop is not that busy, meaning you might get an instructor for yourself or be taught in a small group.

spots.name: Master Divers
spots.desc: A small professional dive PADI 5 Star IDC. They guarantee small groups and offer private tuition and private guiding too. They have an experienced team and time their boat trips to go to dive sites when they are quietest too. They take their diving and environment seriously. They provide free water refills to minimise plastic bottle waste. They re-cycle and provide re-usable containers for…

spots.name: New Way Diving
spots.desc: One of the oldest and most reputable dive shops. This small school has the first dive boat out in the morning. The truck leaves for the harbour at 06:00 to avoid crowds. Small groups, friendly and professional instructors. Basic accommodation is available.

spots.name: Ocean Sound Dive + Yoga
spots.desc: Personal service in small groups. PADI dive courses and 12 scheduled yoga classes per week.

spots.name: PADI IDC Koh Tao
spots.desc: PADI Instructor Courses, full scuba diving internships, gap year programs and lifestyle change.

spots.name: Planet Scuba Koh Tao
spots.desc: 5-star Instructor Development Centre, full range of PADI scuba diving courses for complete beginner all the way through to instructor.

spots.name: Sairee Cottage Diving
spots.desc: PADI scuba diving school on Ko Tao. Very friendly and beautiful diving resort right in the middle of Sairee Beach. Sairee Cottage Diving offers PADI courses from beginner to Scuba Dive IDC Instructor courses including free accommodation.

spots.name: Seashell Dive Centre
spots.desc: Small locally-run shop with helpful multilingual staff, an OK boat and gear, but no free accommodation.

spots.name: Simple Life Divers
spots.desc: Popular medium sized Western-owned and managed PADI 5 star dive centre on Ko Tao's Sairee Beach.

spots.name: ACE Marine Images
spots.desc: All dives and training are offered in small groups with a maximum of 2 divers per 1 staff or private tuition. Specializing in diving for photographers and film makers or those wishing to have a private diving experience. Expeditions are offered on private luxury speedboat or custom-built dive boat and dive schedules change daily to avoid the crowds. Day trips to Ang Thong Marine Park are also…

spots.name: Carabao Diving Center & Resort
spots.desc: A good diving centre on a quiet beach. The staff is gracious and helpful. Good accommodation available.

spots.name: Chalok Reef Divers
spots.desc: SSI dive centre offering beginner courses, advanced training, fun diving and small-group trips around Ko Tao. English-speaking instructors and courses available for both new and experienced divers.

spots.name: Mojo Divers Koh Tao
spots.desc: Friendly dive shop in the heart of Sairee Beach in small groups, fun and friendly atmosphere, from beginners to professional level. Bi-weekly trips to Sail Rock.

spots.name: New Heaven Dive School
spots.desc: Over ten years of experience on Ko Tao. Has been involved with turtle conservation, reef restoration, the We love Ko Tao Festival, the Ko Tao Underwater Festival and other activities which help to create the eco-friendly environment crucial to Ko Tao's future.

spots.name: Koh Exist
spots.desc: A marine conservation school providing information on marine ecology, corals, fish and how to rescue corals by attaching them to artificial structures.

spots.name: Black Tip Diving & Water Sports
spots.desc: Wake boarding, tube rides, shark snorkelling trips, cliff jumping, round the island trips, hiking, kayaking.

spots.name: Bowling and mini golf
spots.desc: The bowling is "manual". There is a guy at the end of the alley that sets up your pins for you after each bowl and returns the ball down to you.

spots.name: Dive Career Internships
spots.desc: Divemaster and dive instructor internships, underwater videographer training, and resort management courses with experienced PADI course instructors.

spots.name: Good Time Adventures, Diving, Beach Cafe and Bar
spots.desc: South Sairee Beach. Small group Scuba Diving courses with flexible schedules. The only shop on Ko Tao with a weekly trip to Sail Rock. A wide range of adventure activities including: rock climbing instruction up to lead climbing and a guiding service, abseiling/rappelling, cliff jumping, snorkelling, wake boarding, boat cruises. Beach Cafe and Bar serves a tasty variety of Western, Thai and…

spots.name: Island Cruises
spots.desc: Day and sunset cruises, private charters, Ang Thong National Marine Park safaris and fully customised crewed charters.

spots.name: Koh Tao PROvideo
spots.desc: A videography company. Run by experienced underwater videographers and instructors who film and teach every day. Each course is tailor made.

spots.name: Monsoon Gym and Muay Thai Camp
spots.desc: For those looking for a serious workout. Muay Thai courses are provided and you can step in the ring for a real bout when you're ready.

spots.name: Oceans Below-underwater Video Training
spots.desc: 3 and 5 day courses in underwater videography and offers professional-level training for those looking to make a career of it. All training done with HD video cameras.

spots.name: Ocean Hiker Sailing Courses
spots.desc: Seamanship courses and competent crew sailing courses Ko Tao-based and liveaboards on ocean-going yacht.

spots.name: Ocean Sound Yoga
spots.desc: Vinyasa, Yin, Meditation, Hatha and Restorative yoga classes offered daily. High quality equipment provided. All levels welcome.

spots.name: Thailand Gap Internships
spots.desc: 1-7 month internships in Pro HD video training, muay Thai, free diving, PADI instructor, divemaster and technical dive courses.

spots.name: Good Idea Massage
spots.desc: Thai massage, oil massage, foot massage, body scrub, reflexology massage. Also waxing hair removal treatments from the face and body – for women and men.

spots.name: Parawan's Thai Home Cooking Classes
spots.desc: Parawan offers Thai cooking classes at her home on Koh Tao and online.

spots.name: 995 Roasted Duck
spots.desc: Simple menu consisting of ten well executed dishes. Their spicy noodle soup with duck (or pork/fish balls) is a Thai local favourite.

spots.name: Bang Burgers
spots.desc: Established by an Australian expatriate, Bang Burgers produces 6 varieties of homemade burgers and 6 varieties of homemade sauces. Open for breakfast with fresh ground espresso from north Thailand. Delivery option available.

spots.name: Cafe del Sol
spots.desc: Authentic French and Italian-style cuisine, home made pasta and pizza, smoked salmon and choice steaks, excellent wine collection and Erdinger weissbier.

spots.name: Choppers Bar and Grill
spots.desc: Australian sports bar. Live music, live sports, pub grub, and a wide selection of beers.

spots.name: Dolce Vita Italian Restaurant
spots.desc: Run by 2 brothers from Apulia, this place offers traditional Italian cuisine in a cosy ambiance. Lavazza coffee, daily home made pasta and authentic pizza, meats from New Zealand, fresh seafood, home-made desserts, wine bar.

spots.name: Farango Pizzeria
spots.desc: Italian-style pizza and pasta, always busy with dine in or take away. Expect to pay 140 baht for pasta or 200 baht for a pizza from the wood-fired oven. Delivery available.

spots.name: Safety Stop Pub
spots.desc: Comfy English pub with tropical beer garden. Draught beers, "wild" buckets. English pub grub. Weekend BBQ's, Sunday roasts, daily specials, live sports.

spots.name: Shalimar Indian Cuisine
spots.desc: Authentic Indian chefs, ingredients, and tandoor. Wide variety of tasty dishes in a beautiful garden setting. Relax in the lounge for cocktails and sheesha. Take away and delivery available.

spots.name: The Snack Shack
spots.desc: Late-night burgers, chicken pita kebabs, hot dogs, falafel, chips (french fries to the non-Brits) available with curry sauce, chili con carne or just good old salt and vinegar. One of only a few places on the island open after 22:00 to get food other than 7-Eleven. Delivery between 22:00-02:00.

spots.name: A Taste of Home
spots.desc: Homemade dishes, large portions, and friendly, relaxed atmosphere made this Trip Advisor's top listed restaurant on Ko Tao.

spots.name: Thipwimarn Restaurant
spots.desc: Wonderful sunset views and a "higher class" feel, but the prices are not much different from the rest of the island. Great for dates.

spots.name: Tony & Aoi Bar/Restaurant
spots.desc: Italian/Thai/English place. Imported Italian pasta starting from 100 baht along with the usual English and Thai fare. New, clean and well-priced, especially for the pasta.

spots.name: Tortoise Burger & Beer
spots.desc: With only five stools, senseless hours, and good music, this place feels like it's been ripped from an alley in Brooklyn. The menu has five options: beef burger, chicken burger, chicken BBQ burger, fish burger, and veggie burger. The veggie burger is homemade and delicious.

spots.name: Zest Cafe
spots.desc: Great for coffee, breakfast, and sandwiches. A favourite with the seasonal dive shop employees. Free Wi-Fi, TV always silently tuned to BBC. Friendly, helpful staff. A second location in Mae Haad.

spots.name: The Castle
spots.desc: Weekly parties at this out-of-the-way club. Can prove to be a good night out with refreshing tunes and a mixed crowd.

spots.name: Dirty Nelly's
spots.desc: First and only Irish pub on Ko Tao with Irish management, live music, extensive food options, and live sport.

spots.name: DJL Bar, Pool & Restaurant
spots.desc: Bar with swimming pool. Friday night pool parties, with free BBQ & shots.

spots.name: Fizz Beach Lounge
spots.desc: Comfy beanbags, awesome sunsets, fantastic cocktail, authentic Thai or Western food and deep, funky house beats.

spots.name: In Touch
spots.desc: Late night club that is open only a couple of times a week. House music.

spots.name: Pub Crawl
spots.desc: Enjoy drink promotions, prizes and join the crowd on a tour of the best bars in Ko Tao.

spots.name: Vibe
spots.desc: Atmospheric beach bar with happy, funky vibes, fire shows & cocktails.

spots.name: The City Wall
spots.local: กำแพงเมือง
spots.desc: The city chronicle already mentions a fortification when the town was reestablished in 1278. Restorations were recorded at the time of King Ramesuan (14th century), as well as King Narai (1686). The latter was aided by the French engineer, M. de la Mare. The walls spread 456 m from east to west, and 2,238 m north to south, enclosing an area of about one square kilometre. The northern wall had…

spots.name: National Museum Nakhon Si Thammarat
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติ นครศรีธรรมราช
spots.desc: The museum has on display artifacts found in four southern provinces, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Phatthalung, Surat Thani, and Chumphon. There is a good collection of rare books and important books sent by the National Library in Bangkok.
spots.addr: ถนนราชดำเนิน, ตำบลในเมือง อำเภอเมือง จังหวัดนครศรีธรรมราช

spots.name: Wat Phra Mahathat
spots.local: วัดพระมหาธาตุวรมหาวิหาร
spots.desc: The most important temple in Nakhon Si Thammarat and southern Thailand. It was constructed at the time of the founding of the town, and contains a tooth relic of Buddha. The 78 m high chedi is surrounded by 173 smaller ones. While the chedi is now in Sri Lankan style, it is said to have been built on top of an earlier Srivijaya-style chedi. At the base of the chedi is a gallery named Viharn Tap…
spots.addr: 435 Ratchadamnoen Rd, Tambon Nai Mueang, Mueang District

spots.name: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan
spots.local: วัดพระมหาธาตุวรมหาวิหาร
spots.desc: A royal temple. Inside the temple are many buildings of importance, especially the royal building which has architecture from the Ayutthaya period and the Sam Chom building where the Buddha image, attired in royal wardrobe Phra Si Thamma Sokarat, is housed.

spots.name: Phra Phutthaishing
spots.local: พระพุทธสิหิงค์
spots.desc: This sacred image was believed to have been ordered by the King of Lanka in 157 CE and was brought to Thailand during the reign of King Ramkhamhaeng the Great. The hall housing the image was originally the Buddha image hall of the palace of Chao Phraya Nakhon (Noi).

spots.name: Ho Phra Isuan
spots.local: หอพระอิศวร
spots.desc: A historical site of the Brahman religion. It has on display the Shiva Linga which is the symbol of Shiva, the Brahman god. There are also several bronze images such as the Siwa Nattarat image, Phra Uma, and Phra Phikkhanet.

spots.name: Ho Phra Narai
spots.local: หอพระนารายณ์
spots.desc: A Brahman place of worship opposite Ho Phra Isuan. A gray sandstone image of the god Narai wearing a hat and holding a conch in the right hand was discovered in the hall.

spots.name: Phra Wihan Sung
spots.local: พระวิหารสูง
spots.desc: The building houses plaster images with a fat clay core. The images are either from the 23rd-24th Buddhist century or from the late-Ayutthaya period.

spots.name: The Thai-style monks' residence of Wat Wang Tawan Tok
spots.local: กุฏิทรงไทยวัดวังตะวันตก
spots.desc: The three houses have a pointed roof connected to the other and there are exquisite Nakhon Si Thammarat designs on the walls, doors, windows, and vents. The Siam Architects Society named these houses the best conservation effort in the area of historical sites and temples in 1992.

spots.name: Wat Chai Na Meditation Centre
spots.local: สำนักวิปัสสนากรรมฐานวัดชายนา
spots.desc: Meditation courses are held for Thais and foreigners. The famous monk Phutthathat Bhikkhu established the centre as a branch of his monastery in Surat Thani.

spots.name: Chinese buildings at Wat Pradu and Wat Chaeng
spots.local: เก๋งจีนวัดประดู่และวัดแจ้ง
spots.desc: Built in the early Rattanakosin period, they house the ashes of Phraya Nakhon and believed to also have the ashes of King Taksin the Great.

spots.name: Chedi Yak
spots.local: เจดีย์ยักษ์
spots.desc: The province’s second-tallest pagoda after Phra Borom That pagoda. It is said that the pagoda was built by Khotkhiri, a wealthy Mon, and his employees when they took refuge in the city in 1003.

spots.name: Residence of Ok Ya Sena Phimuk/Yamada Nagamasa
spots.local: จวนออกญาเสนาภิมุข – ยามาดา นางามาซา
spots.desc: The name of a Japanese volunteer soldier living in the Ayutthaya period during the reign of King Songtham. He was rewarded for his many contributions to the palace by being appointed Ok Ya Sena Phimuk and as the lord of Nakhon Si Thammarat in 1629.

spots.name: Wirathai Monument
spots.local: อนุสาวรีย์วีรไทย
spots.desc: Aade of blackened copper. The locals call this monument Cha Dam or Chao Pho Dam. It was erected to honor Thai soldiers in southern Thailand who died fighting the invading Japanese in World War II on 8 December 1941.

spots.name: Arts and Culture Centre of Nakhon Si Thammarat Rajabhat Institute
spots.local: สำนักศิลปและวัฒนธรรม สถาบันราชภัฏนครศรีธรรมราช
spots.desc: It is the centre of information on archaeological sites discovered in the province. The most important artifacts here are the stone inscriptions found at Khao Chong Khoi and artifacts from the ancient community at Wat Mok Lan.

spots.name: Somdet Phra Sri Nakharin 84 Park
spots.local: สวนสมเด็จพระศรีนครินทร์ 84
spots.desc: Built as part of Ratcharudi Park in the time of King Rama V, the park has an open zoo, a bird park, a health park, and a lake which is home to waterfowl that migrate here during January to March every year.

spots.name: Mueang Nakhon Reception House
spots.local: เรือนรับรองเมืองนคร
spots.desc: Built to receive the king and Crown Princess Maha Chakri when they visited the city. It is in an old fruit orchard of the Thongsamak family which built the house for the royal family on behalf of the city's people.

spots.name: Wat Khao Khun Phanom and the Khao Khun Phanom Scientific Study Centre
spots.local: วัดเขาขุนพนมและศูนย์วิทยาศาสตร์เพื่อการศึกษาเขาขุนพนม
spots.desc: Wat Khao Khun Phanom is a temple of historical and archaeological importance. The temple has a cave lined with brick and marked with heart-shaped stones marking the limits of the temple similar to those along the city wall.

spots.name: Wat Tham Thong Phannara
spots.local: วัดถ้ำทองพรรณรา
spots.desc: It became tradition that on the first full-moon night of the 11th lunar month (October) people would pay homage to the reclining image and the images representing the nuns called Phra Pring and Phra Prang.

spots.name: Khao Kha
spots.local: แหล่งโบราณคดีเขาคา
spots.desc: A sacred religious place of the Saiwanikai sect which worships Shiva as its highest god. Many artifacts used in rites have been found here including phallic symbols, holy water pipes, ruins, and an ancient pond.

spots.name: Wat That Tharam/Wat Khao That
spots.local: วัดธาตุธารามหรือวัดเขาธาตุ
spots.desc: The entire pagoda is made of coral in the shape of an inverted jar. The pagoda is surrounded by Buddha images of red sandstone.

spots.name: Wat Parian
spots.local: วัดป่าเรียน
spots.desc: This new wat has a museum and is founded on remains of an ancient temple where Ganesha statue was found.

spots.name: Museum Honouring the King for the Development of Pak Phanang Basin
spots.local: พิพิธภัณฑ์เฉลิมพระเกียรติเพื่อพัฒนาพื้นที่ลุ่มน้ำปากพนัง
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the king's Project to Develop Pak Phanang Basin in Nakhon Si Thammarat, Phatthalung, and Songkhla.

spots.name: Wat Nantharam
spots.local: วัดนันทาราม
spots.desc: Houses Luang Pho Phut, a red sandstone Buddha image from the Ayutthaya period. In addition, the temple houses a giant phallic symbol found at Khao Kha archaeological site and is believed to be around 1,200 years old. Formerly Wat Tai.

spots.name: Kuan Im Goddess Image
spots.local: พระโพธิสัตว์กวนอิม
spots.desc: A large white plaster image. The image is in the middle of a large pond surrounded by fountains.

spots.name: Thalad Park
spots.desc: A good place to spend a relaxing day. The landscaping is impressive though it is not well maintained. The city museum is near the entrance.

spots.name: Niello ware
spots.local: เครื่องถมนคร
spots.desc: There are two types: black surface with white designs and black surface with gold designs. Niello ware of this province is popular for its durability and intricate designs by hand. The finished product is a bright, shiny black object with beautiful patterns.

spots.name: Yan Li Phao basketry
spots.local: จักสานย่านลิเภา
spots.desc: Yan Li Phao (ย่านลิเภา) is a clinging vine that grows in damp places. It split into threads and woven into beautiful products The trunk is very tough and durable, so locals found a way to make good use of it by making household goods such as handbags, tobacco boxes, and utensils. Locals have been making it for over 100 years. Very nice stuff, but pricey, so don't be bashful about bargaining.

spots.name: Kanom La Nim

spots.desc: A ready-to-eat sweetened flour treat which comes in sheets. It cannot be preserved for more than a week.

spots.name: Kanom La Tod

spots.name: Wat Ratchabophit
spots.local: วัดราชบพิตร
spots.desc: Built by King Rama V in 1869, it was created to keep up with the tradition that each newly-appointed monarch erected a temple to mark his reign. The temple is a mixture of local and Western styles, as the exterior of the chapel is in Thai style, but the interior copies the regal style of European monarchies. A major feature of this wat is the Royal Mausoleum on the west side of the temple…

spots.name: Wat Ratchanaddaram
spots.local: วัดราชนัดดาราม
spots.desc: Wat Ratchanaddaram is a temple compound built by order of King Rama III in 1846. Its main structure, Loh Prasat (โลหะปราสาท, Thai for metal castle), is easily spotted as its spires are of black iron, not the usual glittery gold. It is in a highly unusual style: the wat itself is a five-storied gleaming white structure with rows of Buddhas and nice views from up top, very elegant, calm and…

spots.name: Wat Ratchapradit
spots.local: วัดราชประดิษฐ์สถิตมหาสีมาราม
